Q1.description: Websites/apps can have inconsistent and outdated content on a website/app if the responsibility and ownership of the website/app is not assigned to a person or team.

Q2.description: People may not be able to get the information about the website/app.

Q3.description: Without correct copyright policy, any information on the website/app may be copied, reproduced, republished, uploaded, posted, transmitted, or distributed without any consent.

Q4.description: The overall quality of a website’s content can be degraded if the authenticity and relevance of the ‘linked’ information is not defined through hyperlinking policy.

Q5.description: Without terms and conditions on websites/apps it is difficult to uphold and maintain the trust imposed on them by the users to the sites, the government websites/apps should not out rightly ‘disclaim’ the content of another government website/app.

Q6.description: If Content is not selected keeping the audience in mind, people from diverse professional, educational and demographic backgrounds cannot easily comprehend the same.

Q7.description: People cannot get the right information from the website/app if Content is not up to date, incomplete, inconsistent or scattered.

Q8.description: Users cannot identify an authenticated government website.

Q9.description: Websites/apps with poor design methodology may not be accessible with slow internet connectivity.

Q10.description: Without feedback and help sections, users will not be able to participate in the improvement of website/app quality and the government organisation will not be able to get the information regarding problems faced by users.

A1.description: Visually impaired people cannot access the content.

A2.description: People with epileptic may get seizures if the website/app has content which blink very fast.

A3.description: Hearing/Auditory impaired people cannot access the content.

A4.description: People with cognitive Disability cannot access the time dependent function/content which does not have pause/extend/back/ forward options.

A5.description: People with Locomotor/Physical Disability cannot access the whole content present on the website.

A6.description: If the content is not robust enough to be interpreted reliably by a wide variety of user agents, including assistive technologies, the content becomes inaccessible to large audiences suffering from different impairments.

A7.description: People who do not understand English language cannot access website/app content and services.

A8.description: The government organisation concerned can face legal actions as per national and international laws if the content of the website/app is not accessible.

A9.description: Labels or instructions are not provided when content requires user input, which jeopardises the security or purpose of the content.

S1.description: Malicious users can deface the website.

S2.description: Any harmful actor may get access to confidential information.

S3.description: The availability of the website/app can be hampered.

S4.description: The malicious user may change/modify the content on the website.

S5.description: Security failures typically lead to unauthorised information disclosure, modification, or destruction of all data or performing a business function outside the user’s limits.

S6.description: A file upload flaw allows an attacker to retrieve the password database. Security of web applications determine the protection needs of data in transit and at rest. Attackers can steal such information for example, passwords, credit card numbers, health records, personal information and business secrets require extra protection, mainly if that data falls under privacy laws, Personal data protection bill etc.

S7.description: An attacker monitors network traffic (e.g., at an insecure wireless network), downgrades connections from HTTPS to HTTP, intercepts requests and steals the user’s session cookie. The attacker then replays this cookie and hijacks the user’s (authenticated) session, accessing or modifying the user’s private data. Instead of the above they could alter all transported data, e.g., the recipient of a money transfer.

S8.description: Almost any source of data can be an injection vector, environment variables, parameters, external and internal web services and all types of users. Injection flaws occur when an attacker can send hostile data to an interpreter.

S9.description: Attackers have to gain access to only a few accounts, or just one admin account to compromise the system. Depending on the domain of the application, this may allow unauthorized financial transactions, social security misuse and identity theft, or disclose legally protected highly sensitive information.

S10.description: Security flaws can be used to extract data, execute a remote request from the server, scan internal systems, perform a denial-of-service attack, as well as execute other attacks. The business impact depends on the protection needs of all affected applications and data.

S11.description: Attackers acting as users or administrators, or users using privileged functions, can create, access, update or delete every record.

S12.description: Security misconfiguration frequently gives attackers unauthorised access to some system data or functionality. Occasionally, such flaws result in a complete system compromise.

S13.description: The impact of XSS is moderate for reflected and DOM XSS and severe for stored XSS, with remote code execution on the victim’s browser, such as stealing credentials, sessions, or delivering malware to the victim.

S14.description: While some known vulnerabilities lead to only minor impacts, some of the largest breaches to date have relied on exploiting known vulnerabilities in components.

S15.description: Most successful attacks start with vulnerability probing. Allowing such probes to continue can raise the likelihood of a successful exploit to nearly 100%.

rti_section_24_exemptions.statutory_citation: RTI Act, 2005 Section 24(1), Section 24(4) & The Second Schedule (as amended up to 18 November 2025)
rti_section_24_exemptions.handling_rule: When an audited `.gov.in` hostname belongs to an organisation listed in the Second Schedule (or a State-notified intelligence/security organisation under Section 24(4)), classify RTI Section 4/5/19 checkpoints as `not_applicable_exempt` rather than `not_observed`. checkpoints.title: Government Emblem / Logo Prominence
checkpoints.requirement_text: Association to Government is demonstrated using Emblem/Logo in proper ratio and colour, prominently displayed on the homepage/homescreen of the website/app.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Homepage header emblem/logo image with descriptive alt text.
checkpoints.caveats: Static HTML detects emblem/logo markup and alt text; visual aspect ratio and colour accuracy require visual/agent review.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify visual prominence, proper aspect ratio and colour, and compliance with the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Reassures visitors that the government website/app is authentic and trustworthy. Moreover, the government organisation’s brand identity is reinforced.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Government organisations must select proper visual identity elements like emblems or logos to highlight government ownership of the website/app. The State emblem of India must be displayed on the homepages of the websites and homescreens of the apps of Central Government Ministries/Departments. State Governments should display their Emblems and public Sector organisations and autonomous bodies should display their official logo on the homepage of the website or homescreen of the app to reinforce their identity
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Visual Identity elements (logos and emblem) must prominently stand out on the page, in a proper ratio and colour. Developers must ensure that all logo images are accompanied by proper alternate text so that the screen reader users may be informed of the same. The usage of the State Emblem of India must comply with the provisions of the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Ownership Information & Standalone Subpages
checkpoints.requirement_text: Ownership information is displayed on the homepage/homescreen and on all important entry pages/screens of the website/app and each subsequent page/screen is a standalone entity in terms of ownership, navigation and context of content.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Footer/header ownership statement identifying the owning ministry, department, or state government.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 checks ownership attribution on sampled pages; checking all deep entry pages requires multi-page agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify ownership, navigation, and content context remain standalone on important subpages and entry screens.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Helps to build trust in the visitors and reinforces the government organisation’s branding. Also, search engines use the ownership information to verify the legitimacy of the websites/apps and accord higher ranks in search results.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Provide complete ownership information for publishing on the website
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure display of ownership information, either in the header or footer, on the homepage/homescreen and all-important entry pages/screens of the website/app.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Source Attribution for Reproduced Documents
checkpoints.requirement_text: Source of all documents, not owned by the dept. that have been reproduced in part or full, is mentioned.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Source citations on reproduced reports/documents.
checkpoints.caveats: Identifying whether a published document belongs to another organisation requires semantic reading of content.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect published documents, reports, and excerpts not authored by the owning department to verify source title, authoring organisation, and publication year are cited.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Audiences can rely upon the credibility of authentic information being published by the government organisation. Additionally, giving the credit to the authoring organisation helps establish an environment of respect for intellectual property of other organisations and discourages plagiarism.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: If any published government document/report is being reproduced on the government organisation’s website/app, whether as excerpts or in full, the organisation must cite the source of the same (complete title of the document/report, along with the name of the owner organisation and the year of publication).
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure provision of appropriate data input fields in the CMS to input the source (owner organisation of each published document/report and the year of publication).
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Copyright Permissions for Third-Party Content
checkpoints.requirement_text: Due permissions have been obtained for publishing any content protected by copyright.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Published Copyright Policy page on the website (checked via terms_copyright_link / website_policies_link).
checkpoints.caveats: Internal copyright clearance records and permissions are audited in STQC backend audits and are not public.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Cannot be verified externally from public pages; check published Copyright Policy disclosure under GIGW-L-03.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Publishing copyrighted information after obtaining due permission protects the government organisation from legal issues, establishes an environment of respect for information copyrighted by others in addition to discouraging plagiarism.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must follow proper procedures to obtain the permission, prior to publishing any information that is copyrighted by any third party.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: None.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall check the implementation of copyright policy in backend audit.

checkpoints.title: Last Updated / Reviewed Date on Homepage
checkpoints.requirement_text: Homepage/homescreen of website displays the last updated/reviewed date.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Footer/header 'Last Updated on <date>' or 'Last Reviewed on <date>' notice.
checkpoints.caveats: Date indicators rendered solely via client-side JavaScript or regional-script date words outside regex patterns may show as not_observed.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Check whether the displayed date is fresh relative to actual site updates and present on key entry pages.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Providing information about the last updated/reviewed date helps visitors to build trust that the government organisation is providing updated information. Also, search engines accord a higher ranking to web sites that publish updated content, so they will automatically appear amongst the top-ranking sites on search results.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Publish regular and updated content for publishing on the website/app and review the content of the website/app as per the content review policy.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure publishing, on the homepage/homescreen and every important entry page/screen, of the date on which the information was posted on the website/app, or the date on which the content was last reviewed and/or modified.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Downloadable Material Metadata (Title, Size, Format, Instructions)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Complete information including title, size, format and usage instructions is provided for all downloadable material.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Inline file format and size labels next to PDF/document download links (e.g. '(PDF, 1.2 MB)').
checkpoints.caveats: Sites with zero downloadable links on the homepage return unassessable for this static indicator; usage instructions and malware screening require deeper/backend review.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify downloadable files include self-explanatory titles, exact file size, format, and viewer/usage instructions across downloads sections.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Downloading material from the Internet can be an expensive and time-consuming exercise. Therefore, government websites/apps must provide Information that will help visitors determine whether they want to access downloadable material. Providing all required information about downloadable material helps improve clarity & accessibility, especially for those using assistive technologies.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Provide all necessary content details to the content team. The total size of the file should be kept to a minimum to ensure acceptable download times for all users, especially those that do not have high-speed, reliable Internet connections. Prior to making downloadable material available for visitors, government organisations should check for viruses and malware.
guidelines_detail.developer_action:
Ensure that there is a mechanism in the CMS to input the following information about the downloadable material:
Self explanatory title of the document/file.
Download and use instructions (install, open, view).
File format and file size.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Metadata for Circulars, Notifications, Schemes, Forms & Notices
checkpoints.requirement_text:
With respect to each, Circular, Notification, Document, Form, Scheme, Service and Recruitment notice, the following should be clearly listed on the Website:
- Complete title
- Language (if other than English)
- Purpose/procedure to apply (as applicable)
- Validity (if applicable)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Structured metadata columns or tags on Circulars/Schemes/Tenders/Recruitment listings.
checkpoints.caveats: Evaluating completeness of all 4 attributes across domain-specific notices requires agent reading.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect public Circulars, Notifications, Schemes, Services, Forms, and Recruitment pages to check whether each lists: (a) complete title, (b) language if non-English, (c) purpose/procedure to apply, and (d) validity date.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Details such as the correct title, language, validity, purpose, procedures would lead to an accurate search output for information on that scheme/service/recruitment notice etc and it would be easy for the users to locate & use these documents, schemes, services etc.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The attributes as specified in the guideline must be provided with each Circular, Notification, Document, Form, Scheme, Service and Recruitment notice
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure provision of all fields necessary for publishing of all information about documents, schemes, services, along with the necessary archival procedures to archive the information once the validity expires.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Removal or Archival of Outdated Notices & Tenders
checkpoints.requirement_text: All outdated Announcements, Tenders, Recruitment notices, News and Press Releases are removed from the website and/or placed into the archives as per the archival policy.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Presence of an Archives section and absence of long-expired tenders/notices in active feeds.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires comparing notice expiry dates against current date and verifying archival separation.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect active Announcements, Tenders, Recruitments, News, and Press Releases sections to verify expired items have been moved to an Archives section rather than left live.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Outdated and irrelevant content must not be served to the visitors and there should be a proper archival section to access the outdated content.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must ensure that the expiry date is provided for all time sensitive content
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure that the mechanism is in place to automatically remove the content after the expiry date or move it to the archives as per the approved Archival Policy.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Comprehensive 'About Us' Section & Update Mechanism
checkpoints.requirement_text: All information about the government organisation, useful for the citizen and other stakeholders, is present in the ‘About Us’ section and a mechanism is in place to keep the information up to date.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Prominent 'About Us' link and organisational overview page.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 observes link presence; substantive completeness of About Us content requires agent inspection and internal update workflows require backend audit.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect the linked About Us page for completeness (mandate, organisational structure, functions); backend update mechanism is an STQC backend check.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Helps the visitor access all information about the government organisation, useful for the citizen.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must prepare the content describing itself for the About us section.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure the website/app has an About us page.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying the content as required by this checkpoint is present on the website. The evaluator shall verify the conformity to the mechanism required in the checkpoint through backend audit.

checkpoints.title: 'Contact Us' Page with Functionary Details
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website has a ‘Contact Us’ page providing complete contact details of important functionaries in the government organisation and this is linked from the homepage/homescreen and all relevant places on the website/app.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Contact Us / Directory link with official email, postal address, and telephone indicators.
checkpoints.caveats: Image-only contact cards, JS-rendered directories, or unlabelled addresses may appear as not_observed; W1 never stores raw phone/email/address strings.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect the Contact Us / Who's Who page to verify key citizen-facing functionaries, designations, public-dealing timings, and official @gov.in/@nic.in contacts are complete.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Enables users to contact any government organisation or entity to ask questions, get information, seek clarifications and resolve problems.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Provide complete contact information on the Contact us or Who’s who sections or on the Directory page, including the telephone numbers/fax numbers, postal address and email addresses, along with the timings, if any, earmarked for personal/public dealing.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure that the CMS has the provision to publish the contact details of citizen-facing functionaries in the government organisation.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: Online Feedback Form & Timely Response Mechanism
checkpoints.requirement_text: Feedback is collected through online forms and a mechanism is in place to ensure timely response to feedback/queries received through the website.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Homepage/footer 'Feedback' link to an online feedback submission form.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 checks link/form presence without submitting any form (strictly read-only); agency response turnaround is internal governance.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Check that the Feedback link opens a working structured online form (without broken endpoints); timely response processing is a backend governance audit.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Helps the visitors to express their ideas, satisfaction levels, suggestions etc. that can be valuable inputs for enhancement of future versions of the website. Additionally, government organisations can learn meaningful insights about the usage pattern of the website, which can further help to focus on near and far term enhancements.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Ensure feedback received is processed on a regular basis.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure providing the mechanism to collect structured feedback from visitors using Forms. Also, ensure responding to the feedback explaining how it will be processed.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying that the feedbacks are collected through online forms at the website. The evaluator shall verify the conformity to the mechanism required in the checkpoint through backend audit.

checkpoints.title: Prominent Link to National Portal (india.gov.in) Opening in New Window
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website provides a prominent link to the ‘National Portal’ from the homepage and subsequent pages belonging to the National Portal load in the new browser window.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Footer/banner link or badge pointing to https://www.india.gov.in/.
checkpoints.caveats: Links injected solely via client-side JavaScript or pointing via redirectors may not be detected in static HTML.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify the National Portal logo/link is prominently visible and opens in a new browser tab/window on subsequent pages too.

guidelines_detail.benefit: india.gov.in, the National Portal of India (NPI) is a single window source for access to all information and services being provided by the various constituents of the Indian Government to its citizens and other stakeholders. Linking to the NPI will help visitors find information or services they could not find easily on a government organisation website
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation website/app must provide a prominent link to the National Portal from the homepage and other important pages of citizen’s interest.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure that the government website/app provides a prominent link to the National Portal from the homepage and other important pages of citizen’s interest. Also, the hyperlinked pages belonging to the National Portal must load into a newly opened browser window of visitors.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Cross-Browser & Regional Font Rendering Compatibility
checkpoints.requirement_text: The website has been tested on multiple browsers. Hindi/Regional language fonts have been tested on popular browsers for any inconsistency (loss of layout).
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: UTF-8 charset declaration and readable Unicode regional script.
checkpoints.caveats: True cross-browser layout fidelity requires rendered browser testing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Render the portal across viewports/browsers and verify Hindi/regional-language Unicode text renders cleanly without garbled glyphs or broken layout (no legacy Kruti Dev/non-Unicode font dependency).

guidelines_detail.benefit: Visitors can easily read content and interact with the website in their native language, thus improving the website’s accessibility and reach.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure use of Unicode characters when using Hindi/Regional language fonts & also, testing of the website on multiple browsers and versions of browsers, operating systems, connection speeds and screen resolutions to ensure access by all and no loss of layout.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website on different browsers for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Readily Available 'Help' Section Linked From All Pages
checkpoints.requirement_text: The website has a readily available Help section linked from all pages of the website.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Footer/header 'Help' link across pages.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 verifies presence on homepage; consistent presence across all subpages and content usefulness require agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Check that the Help page explains file formats/viewers, site navigation, and accessibility help, and is linked consistently on subpages.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Allows a pleasant experience while browsing the website.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Must include Help content which allows for an easy and convenient navigation for the visitor to the website/app (e.g., online help, how to open files of certain formats, how to access audio/video on the portal, kinds of plug-ins required etc.). Further, the content which clarifies the purpose of the website/app as well as its policies for the visitors should also be included in this category. Help should be linked from all pages of the website/app and should be displayed in a consistent location across the website.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website/app for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: CSS-Driven Layout & Responsive Design
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website uses Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) to control layouts/styles and incorporates responsive design features to ensure that the interface displays well on different screen sizes.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Viewport meta tag and stylesheet links in HTML <head>.
checkpoints.caveats: Presence of viewport meta and CSS indicates responsive setup; actual visual responsiveness requires rendered viewport checks.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify the layout adapts cleanly across mobile (320px–390px), tablet, and desktop screen sizes without overflow.

guidelines_detail.benefit: For the visitors, a consistent look and feel of the website’s User Interface (UI)and its availability on all devices and screen sizes is important. For the government organisation and developers, CSS offers ease of making global changes to the layout and design in one place instead of having to do so on individual pages. Different presentations of the content (for example a large text alternative for visually impaired users) can be achieved using different style sheets. The document code is also reduced in size and complexity since it does not need to contain any presentational markup.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Use CSS for controlling content layout and presentation, in addition to offering a responsive interface for visitors. Also, ensure testing on different devices.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall test the website by using browser extension/ tool for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Readability Without Stylesheets (CSS Off)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website is readable even when style sheets are switched off or not loaded.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Logical semantic HTML document structure without CSS-dependent text injection.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires human/agent readability inspection with stylesheets disabled.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Disable CSS (or inspect raw semantic DOM order) to verify content remains logically ordered, readable, and navigable without overlapping or hidden primary text.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Helps provide readable content not only for visually challenged users who may be using screen readers, but also in some instances where the style sheets may not load swiftly or load at all due to reasons such as slow connections, technical errors, or due to use of some incompatible mobile devices.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure testing on different devices to ensure the website remains easily readable even on turning off style sheets.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall test the website by using browser extension/ tool for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Proper Page Title, Language Attribute & Page Metadata
checkpoints.requirement_text: Proper page title and language attribute along with metadata for page like keywords and description are appropriately included.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: HTML <title>, <html lang>, <meta name='description'>, and <meta name='keywords'>.
checkpoints.caveats: Static check validates presence and non-default values; semantic accuracy of keywords/descriptions benefits from agent review.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Check that metadata accurately describes the specific department and subpage topics rather than generic CMS defaults.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Once details such as government organisation name, services offered, schemes, location, help ensure enhanced accessibility, especially for those with screen readers who rely on things such as page titles, structured page headings and lists. Additionally, search engines rank such sites higher in search results.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must provide the relevant metadata for each page.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Must ensure mentioning all necessary metadata in the portion of the html page from where it is read by search engines.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall test the website by using browser extension tools for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Prescribed Minimum Content on Homepage & Subsequent Pages
checkpoints.requirement_text: Minimum content as prescribed in the guidelines is present on the homepage/homescreen and all subsequent pages/screens.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Presence of standard GIGW homepage header/footer minimum-content elements.
checkpoints.caveats: Evaluating citizen-service links and subsequent-page breadcrumb/parent links across the site requires agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify all 10 homepage minimum-content items (including links to major modules and citizen services) plus all 5 subsequent-page minimum-content items (self-explanatory title, homepage link, parent section link, ownership, Contact Us link).

guidelines_detail.benefit: The homepage/homescreen being the primary entry page to the entire content of the website/app should allow visitors to get access to the most important content elements from the homepage/homescreen itself. Often, visitors may use a search engine for finding some information and, therefore, directly reach a subsequent page/screen of the website/app instead of the homepage/homescreen, therefore, it helps to have some minimum content on each page/screen of website/app, e.g., self-explanatory title, link to homepage/homescreen, ownership, link to Contact us etc.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure providing the minimum content as prescribed by the GIGW guidelines referred on the homepage/homescreen as well as the subsequent pages/screens.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test it for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Proper Markup & Header Tags on Data Tables
checkpoints.requirement_text: Data tables have been provided with necessary tags/markup.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Semantic <th>/<thead>/<caption> markup on published HTML data tables.
checkpoints.caveats: Pages without HTML tables return unassessable for this static indicator; distinguishing layout tables from data tables benefits from agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify tables are not used for page layout and that complex data tables associate every data cell with row/column headers (th/scope/headers).

guidelines_detail.benefit: Proper use of markup in tables helps with accessibility, ensuring assistive technology users can easily navigate and comprehend the tabular content.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Avoid use of tables for page layout. Proper tags and markup must be provided to identify row and column headers and associate data cells and header cells.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall test the website by using browser extension/ tool for verifying compliance to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: A4 Printability of Web Page Content
checkpoints.requirement_text: Content of the web page prints correctly on an A4 size paper.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Print stylesheet (@media print) or clean A4 print preview without clipping.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered browser print-layout inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Test print preview / @media print rendering on A4 paper to ensure content is not clipped horizontally or obscured by fixed banners/navbars.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Offers enhanced accessibility to visitors who may prefer the print format.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure testing with font properties such that the text must print correctly on an A4 size paper.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Official .gov.in / .nic.in Domain Usage
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website is in the nic.in or gov.in domain. Educational Institutions and Research and Academic Institutions, which are eligible for registration under ‘gov.in’ may use ‘edu.in’, ‘res.in’ or ‘ac.in’ domains.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Canonical HTTPS URL on .gov.in (or .nic.in / eligible .edu.in, .res.in, .ac.in).
checkpoints.caveats: Inventory already filters to .gov.in hosts; this check catches off-domain redirects or canonical-host drift.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify key citizen services and linked sub-portals do not silently hand users off to unofficial private domains.

guidelines_detail.benefit: The URL or the Web Address of any Government website is a strong indicator of its authenticity and status as being official. Use of gov.in or nic.in domain inspires trust in the visitor that the website being visited is authentic.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must obtain ‘gov.in’ or ‘nic.in’ domain exclusively allotted and restricted to government websites. The domain name conventions, as specified in the ‘.IN Registration’ policy, should be followed while registering a ‘gov.in’ Domain Name. For detailed information and step-by-step procedure on how to register a gov.in Domain visit http://registry.gov.in.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: None
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: API Integration with Key National Government Platforms
checkpoints.requirement_text: API integration with key government platforms (India Portal, DigiLocker, Aadhaar, Single-Sign-On, MyGov, Data Platform, MyScheme) and similar websites of the government organisation must be enabled for seamless exchange of Information and data.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Public links, badges, or login/document flows referencing DigiLocker, Jan Parichay SSO, MyGov, MyScheme, or data.gov.in.
checkpoints.caveats: Applicability depends on the specific department's services (informational sites need different integrations than transactional portals).
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect citizen services and authentication flows to evaluate whether applicable national platforms (India Portal, DigiLocker, Aadhaar/eSign, Jan Parichay SSO, MyGov, data.gov.in, MyScheme) are integrated where relevant to the agency's mandate.

guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must identify the websites and platforms with which the integration needs to be established as per the requirement and no duplication efforts are being made. Provide required APIs and Web Services to the developer/entity to enable integration.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developers must ensure that the integration is done as per the best practices pertaining to security and technology.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Consistent UX & Visual Identity Across Organisation Properties
checkpoints.requirement_text: The government organisation must ensure a consistent user experience and visual identities across all its websites/apps.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Consistent header, branding, and navigation templates across the organisation's web presence.
checkpoints.caveats: Cross-property UX consistency cannot be assessed from a single homepage HTML fetch.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Compare visual branding, navigation terminology, and information architecture across pages of the website and sibling subdomains under the same ministry/state.

guidelines_detail.benefit: IMaintaining consistency enhances the ease of use for the visitors. If the visitors have browsed one website/app then the learning curve of using the other websites/apps of the government organisation is greatly reduced and visitors can interact and find information easily and quickly. Maintaining a consistent visual identity reinforces the authenticity and enhances the trust level of the visitors.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must ensure a consistent information architecture, navigation scheme, terminology and visual branding (logos, etc.) across the web initiatives of all organisations under them.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developers must create templates with common Information Architecture (IA), configurable components and neat user interface, which can be implemented on different websites/apps to achieve consistency.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Integration with Popular Social Media Platforms
checkpoints.requirement_text: Websites/apps must provide integration with popular social media.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Official social media icons/links or feeds on the homepage.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 checks social platform link presence; verifying active two-way content push requires agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify linked social accounts belong to the official organisation and two-way sharing/embeds function properly.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Users and the government organisation are increasingly using social media to quickly connect, share information and even provide services. Social media platforms also provide an easy means of two-way communication between the user and government organisation. Younger generation also finds it easy to connect through social media on smart devices rather than the web interface.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must identify the information/content that needs to be pushed to the social media platforms directly from the websites/apps. The content must also be written in a way that is suitable for social media.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developer must ensure a two-way integration by providing a mechanism to push content from the website/app to the social media platform and also integrate the social media content into the website/app.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for verifying conformity to this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Spelling and Grammatical Accuracy
checkpoints.requirement_text: The language is free from spelling and grammatical errors.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Clean, proofread copy on homepage and key informational pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Multilingual Indian government terminology and proper nouns require LLM/human linguistic evaluation rather than naive spellcheck.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Review English and Hindi/regional-language copy on key public pages for spelling, grammar, and broken translation artifacts.

guidelines_detail.benefit: The language used in a government website/app is very important for ensuring effective communication with the target audiences. When website/app visitors get clear and error free content, it raises the trust level of the citizens towards the government organisation.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Check the content manually or with automated spelling and grammar tools before publishing.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure provision of a CMS that enables publishing of error free content both with respect to grammar and spellings.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall test the website/app by using a tool for verifying conformity to this checkpoint. The evaluator shall check in the backend audit for implementation of the mechanism by verifying documented records.

checkpoints.title: Nominated Web Information Manager (WIM) & Public Details
checkpoints.requirement_text: The government organisation has nominated a WIM as defined in the guidelines.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Published 'Web Information Manager' section or entry on Contact Us / About / Website Policies page.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 detects public WIM text/link on sampled pages without storing personal PII; formal nomination rank and WQM verification are internal governance.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify WIM contact details are clearly published and check whether a senior official (Joint Secretary level or equivalent) is designated; internal nomination order & WIM competence interview are STQC backend audits.

guidelines_detail.benefit: WIM can ensure a proper flow of content to the website/app and ensure that content quality and user satisfaction issues are taken care of. WIM will achieve this by coordinating with the various groups within the government organisation and undertaking multiple activities with regard to the Indian Government website being maintained by her/him. For instance, formulating policies for content management to update authentic content and manage it through the entire life cycle, e.g., creation, moderation, approval, publishing and archival getting the website certified for guidelines conformity and ensuring conformity throughout its lifecycle.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must appoint a WIM who must be a senior official not below the rank of a Joint Secretary (JS).
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Display complete contact details of the WIM on the website, so that visitors could contact him/her in case of some queries or requirements.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will check the website for WIM details and will compare the same with the WIM details in Website Quality Manual (WQM). Further during the backend audit the evaluator will interview WIM to assess his/ her awareness and competence regarding the responsibilities.

checkpoints.title: Website URL Displayed on Stationery & Public Advertisements
checkpoints.requirement_text: It has been ensured that all stationery of the government organisation as well as advertisements/public messages issued by the government organisation concerned prominently display the URL of the web site.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Website URL printed on downloadable official Annual Reports, press releases, and tender PDFs.
checkpoints.caveats: Physical stationery (letterheads, visiting cards, print/AV advertisements) can only be inspected in an STQC backend audit.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Cannot be verified from the website HTML alone; optionally check published official PDFs (Annual Reports, tender notices, press releases) for consistent inclusion of the official website URL.

guidelines_detail.benefit: By mentioning the URL prominently on all stationery and publicity material of the government organisation, the Website can be promoted to attract visitors who may benefit from the information and services being delivered by the government organisation.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must ensure publishing of government website URL prominently on all stationery and publicity materials such as letterheads, visiting cards, publicity material such as brochures, pamphlets and documents such as the annual report etc; advertisements, press releases, tender notifications etc. issued in the newspapers/ audio-visual media. Also, ensure publishing regular and updated news related to the Government and in the interest of the citizens to attract citizens.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Promote government websites/apps by linking with other government websites/apps as well as international websites. Provision may be provided on the website/apps to send regular updates on the website/app through an electronic newsletter to registered and interested users.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will check during the backend audit by examining the stationery (e.g., letterhead, tender document, email signature, Visiting Cards, Publicity material such as Brochures, Pamphlets and documents such as the Annual Report etc; Advertisements, Press Releases, Tender Notifications etc.) conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: 10 Approved Website Policies & Plans (Citizen-Facing Policies Published)
checkpoints.requirement_text:
Website has the following clearly defined policies and plans approved by the WIM.
- Copyright Policy
- Content Contribution, Moderation and Approval (CMAP) policy
- Content Archival (CAP) policy
- Content Review (CRP) policy
- Hyper linking Policy
- Privacy Policy
- Terms & Conditions
- Website Monitoring Plan.
- Contingency Management Plan
- Security Policy
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Footer 'Website Policies' link covering Copyright, Hyperlinking, Privacy, Terms & Conditions, Content Archival (CAP), Content Review (CRP), and CMAP.
checkpoints.caveats: WIM approval signatures, Website Quality Manual (WQM) consistency, and internal operational plans (Website Monitoring Plan, Contingency Management Plan) require backend STQC audit.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Read the linked Website Policies page(s) to check which of the 10 GIGW policies/plans are publicly documented vs missing or placeholder templates; internal WIM approval & operational logs for Monitoring/Contingency Plans are backend governance.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Having clearly defined policies helps ensure efficient management of the website and its content throughout the life cycle of the website.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Clearly define and approve the website related policies listed above. WIM must ensure their implementation throughout the website life cycle
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Citizen-facing policies like copyright policy, privacy policy and terms and conditions must be published on the website.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action:
The evaluator will:
Compare during the backend audit the policies given in WQM and those available at the website for consistency; and
Check the implementation of these policies by examining the documented records generated by the implementation.

checkpoints.title: Hyperlinked Content Accuracy & External Non-Govt Link Alerts
checkpoints.requirement_text: The mechanism is in place to check the accuracy of Hyperlinked Content and clear indications are given when a link leads out to a non-government website.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Published Hyperlinking Policy and external-link icon/new-window warning on non-government links.
checkpoints.caveats: JavaScript confirmation modals and internal accuracy-review workflows require browser/backend inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify external non-government links display a clear user alert/indication when leaving the government website and check published Hyperlinking Policy; internal periodic link-accuracy verification logs are backend governance.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Hyperlinking content across different websites/apps can occasionally cause ambiguity in the mind of the visitors about the owner of a particular portion of content and whom to be contacted in case of any query. Therefore, it helps to verify content accuracy before linking to an external website and thereafter clearly indicating when a visitor is being led to an external website.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Define the Hyperlinking policy, duly approved by the WIM. Check the accuracy of the linked content regularly.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure alert mechanism to notify the visitor when clicking any link will lead to an external website
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action:
The evaluator will check that:
The policy defined in WQM is consistent with that available on the website; and
The mechanism is completely and correctly defined in WQM and the same has been implemented by examining the documented records generated by the implementation.

checkpoints.title: Content Moderation & Approval Against Offensive/Discriminatory Language
checkpoints.requirement_text: It is ensured through content moderation and approval policy that Website content is free from offensive/discriminatory language.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Published CMAP statement under Website Policies (checked via website_policies_link).
checkpoints.caveats: CMS moderation workflow roles (Contributor/Moderator/Approver) and approval audit trails are internal governance audited in STQC backend reviews.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Check if a CMAP (Content Contribution, Moderation & Approval Policy) is published on the Website Policies page and sample public copy for neutral, non-discriminatory civic language.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Content that is free from offensive/discriminatory language helps in promoting inclusivity and enhances the user experience, attracting visitors to frequent the website/app for information and services they gain from.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Any information in text, visual or any other media which may offend/harm the National sentiments as well as security and integrity of the country must be avoided on the website. The government organisations must designate the officials who will implement the content moderation and approval policy (content creator, moderator and/or approver) as required.
guidelines_detail.developer_action:
Ensure CMS has an in-built workflow for content moderation and approval.
has been implemented.
Randomly picked contents fulfil the policy.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action:
The evaluator will check that:
The policy defined in WQM provides commitment to ensure that the website content is free from offensive/ discriminatory language.

checkpoints.title: Simultaneous Updates Across Multilingual Versions
checkpoints.requirement_text: Documents/Pages in multiple languages are updated simultaneously.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Matching 'Last Updated' dates and current notices across language versions.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires loading and comparing multiple language trees semantically.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Compare English and Hindi/regional-language versions of the homepage and key notices to check whether last-updated dates and major announcements stay synchronised or indicate untranslated status.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Helps avoid inconsistencies, at any point, between the various language versions, thus offering visitors the same content in multiple languages.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure mechanism for publishing content in multiple languages and to display the status of non-translated content.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall check the website contents manually to see conformity with this.

checkpoints.title: No Broken Links or 'Page Not Found' (404) Errors
checkpoints.requirement_text: Mechanism is in place to ensure that there are no ‘broken links’ (internal as well as external) or ‘Page not found’ errors.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: All primary homepage navigation and footer links resolve cleanly with HTTP 200.
checkpoints.caveats: Full site-wide link crawling across 12,537 domains would violate polite crawling bounds; W1 checks only bounded primary pages.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Sample key navigation and footer links politely to detect broken internal/external links or 404 errors; internal WQM automated link-monitoring records are backend governance.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Presence of broken links and page not found errors will frustrate the visitors and reduce the trust level of citizens
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Define the Hyperlinking policy, duly approved by the Web Information Manager/p>
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure that ‘broken links’ or those leading to ‘Page Not Found’ errors are checked on a regular basis and are rectified or removed from the website immediately upon discovery. Use appropriate technology tools available for convenient discovery of broken links.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall check that the mechanism is completely and correctly defined in the WQM and verify the implementation by examining the documented records generated by the implementation of the mechanism. Further the evaluator shall also test the website using the tool to check broken links on the website.

checkpoints.title: No Links to 'Under Construction' Pages
checkpoints.requirement_text: There are no links to ‘under construction’ pages.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Absence of 'Under Construction' / 'Coming Soon' placeholder notices.
checkpoints.caveats: W1 inspects sampled pages only; placeholder pages hidden deeper in submenus require agent spot-checking.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Spot-check major menu items to verify sections lead to real content rather than 'Under Construction' / 'Coming Soon' stubs.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Visitors have a better experience when they find content versus experiencing “under construction” pages that convey a negative impression.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Avoid any “under construction” pages as much as possible. Also, the government organisation must provide a date in case the content is event based i.e., Republic Day speech of President
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Avoid publishing any pages with “under construction” / “work in progress”
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Documents Provided in HTML or Accessible Formats
checkpoints.requirement_text: Documents are provided either in HTML or other accessible formats.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: HTML equivalents or text-selectable tagged PDFs for key citizen documents.
checkpoints.caveats: Checking whether linked PDFs are OCR-ed/tagged vs image-only scans requires downloading and inspecting document internals.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Inspect linked circulars, acts, forms, and reports to check whether content is published in HTML or tagged/text-searchable accessible PDFs rather than inaccessible scanned image-only PDFs.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Enhanced accessibility for all website visitors, especially the visually challenged who should be able to use assistive technologies to read the accessible format documents.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must ensure that the accessible version of all scanned documents is made available
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure uploading of documents in HTML or other accessible formats.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually test the website for this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: Bilingual Portal with Prominent Language Selector & Unicode
checkpoints.requirement_text: Website is bilingual with a prominent language selection link and uses Unicode characters.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: UTF-8 charset and prominent header language switcher (e.g. हिन्दी / regional language).
checkpoints.caveats: W1 checks encoding and language-selector markup; verifying real translated content parity is covered under GIGW-L-06.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify switching language actually loads translated Unicode content (not an empty or broken mirror) and check whether a preferred-language selector is prominent on entry.

guidelines_detail.benefit: India is a country with diverse cultures and as many as 22 languages. This will enable wider use of websites/apps by the rich Indian demographics, a large part which is more comfortable in regional languages versus English.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Provide resources to translate all content. If difficult, determine which content is widely accessed by visitors and translate those sections to regional language.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure use of Unicode character set for regional language content and thorough testing to ensure access by all and no loss of layout. Provide users with an option to select their preferred language (e.g. through a pop up) prior to entering the website.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator shall manually and through tool test the website for this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.1.1: Non-text Content
checkpoints.requirement_text: All non-text content that is presented to the user has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose, except for the situations listed below.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: All elements carry appropriate alt attributes.
checkpoints.caveats: Static check verifies alt attribute presence; semantic quality of descriptions and non-image media alternatives require agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify alt text is meaningful (not generic 'image'/'banner'), decorative images use alt='', and CAPTCHAs provide accessible audio/alternative modes.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Conformity makes information conveyed by non-text content accessible through the use of a text alternative. For example, a person who cannot see a picture can have the text alternative read aloud using synthesised speech. A person who cannot hear an audio file can have the text alternative displayed so that he or she can read it.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: A meaningful explanatory text equivalent must be specified for images and other non-text content. The description should summarise the content or purpose of the image. For example, to use the description ‘Picture’ to explain a graphic does not serve any purpose.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/ accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.2.1: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
checkpoints.requirement_text:
For pre-recorded audio-only and pre-recorded video-only media, the following are true, except when the audio or video is a media alternative for text and is clearly labelled as such:
- Pre-recorded Audio-only: An alternative for time-based media is provided that presents equivalent information for pre-recorded audio-only content.
- Pre-recorded Video-only: Either an alternative for time-based media or an audio track is provided that presents equivalent information for pre-recorded video-only content.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.2.1 (Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: The intent of this Success Criterion is to make information conveyed by pre-recorded audio-only and pre-recorded video-only content available to all users. Alternatives for time-based media that are text based make information accessible because text can be rendered through any sensory modality (for example, visual, auditory or tactile) to match the needs of the user.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Create the alternate for time-based media, i.e, transcript in case audio only and transcript or audio track in case of video only content. Captions are not needed when the synchronised media is, itself, an alternate presentation of information that is also presented via text on the Web page
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Make provision to provide alternatives for time-based media.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.2.2: Captions (Prerecorded)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Captions are provided for all pre-recorded audio content in synchronised media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labelled as such.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.2.2 (Captions (Prerecorded)) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test the it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: This enables people who are deaf or hard of hearing to watch synchronised media presentations.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must create captions to provide the part of the content available via the audio track. Captions not only include dialogue but identify who is speaking and include non-speech information conveyed through sound, including meaningful sound effects.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Ensure that the captions are available with audio content.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test the it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.2.3: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
checkpoints.requirement_text: An alternative for time-based media or audio description of the pre-recorded video content is provided for synchronised media, except when the media is a media alternative for text and is clearly labelled as such.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.2.3 (Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test the it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: provides people who are blind or visually impaired access to the visual information in a synchronised media presentation
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisations must provide audio description of the video content. The audio description augments the audio portion of the presentation with the information needed when the video portion is not available. Alternatively, all of the information in the synchronised media (both visual and auditory) may be provided in text form. If all of the information in the video track is already provided in the audio track, no audio description is necessary.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developer must provide provision for publishing the alternative for time-based media or audio description of the pre-recorded video content
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test the it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.2.4: Captions (Live)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Captions are provided for all live audio content in synchronised media.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.2.4 (Captions (Live)) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Enables people who are deaf or hard of hearing to watch real-time presentations.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: The government organisation must provide captions for live audio content.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Provide provision to publish captions
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.2.5: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Audio description is provided for all pre-recorded video content in synchronised media.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.2.5 (Audio Description (Prerecorded)) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually a check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Provides people who are blind or visually impaired access to the visual information in a synchronised media presentation. During existing pauses in dialogue, audio description provides information about actions, characters, scene changes and on-screen text that are important and are not described or spoken in the main soundtrack.
guidelines_detail.government_organisation_action: Provide Audio description of pre-recorded video content
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Provide provision to publish audio description
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually a check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.3.1: Info and Relationships
checkpoints.requirement_text: Information, structure and relationships conveyed through presentation can be programmatically determined or are available in text.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Semantic HTML5 landmarks (<main>, <nav>, <header>, <footer>) and heading hierarchy.
checkpoints.caveats: Presence of landmarks/headings is a necessary static indicator; full programmatic-vs-visual fidelity requires agent inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Verify heading hierarchy, lists, form fieldsets/labels, and table structures programmatically match visual presentation.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Sighted users perceive structure and relationships through various visual cues present on a page (page headings are in a larger and bold font; list items are preceded by a bullet; form fields may be positioned as groups that share text labels; a different background colour may be used to indicate related items and so on). However, visually challenged users cannot take advantage of these cues. It must be ensured that these information and relationships are preserved even when the presentation format changes. (For example, when the content is read by a screen reader or CSS is turned off or replaced).
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developers must ensure that information and relationships that are implied by visual or auditory formatting are preserved when the presentation format changes. For example, when the content is read by a screen reader or when a user style sheet is substituted for the style sheet provided by the author. For example, a form contains several required fields. The labels for the required fields are displayed in red. In addition, at the end of each label is an asterisk character (*). The instructions for completing the form indicate that “all required fields are displayed in red and marked with an asterisk *”, followed by an example.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.3.2: Meaningful Sequence
checkpoints.requirement_text: When the sequence in which content is presented affects its meaning, a correct reading sequence can be programmatically determined.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.3.2 (Meaningful Sequence) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: This helps people who rely on assistive technologies like screen readers because the meaning evident in the sequencing of the information in the visual presentation will be the same when the content is presented in spoken form. This also preserves the meaning of the page when the CSS is turned off or not supported.
guidelines_detail.developer_action:
Provide a meaningful reading sequence.
Note: Developers must keep in mind that a sequence is meaningful if change of order shall impact its meaning. Two independent content items like two separate articles in a page may be placed in any sequence without affecting the meaning. Similarly, the navigation block and the content area may be placed in any sequence without affecting their meaning. HTML text is always a meaningful sequence. Tables and ordered lists are meaningful sequences, but unordered lists are not. It must be clear that providing a particular linear order is only required where it affects meaning There may be more than one order that is “correct” and only one correct order needs to be provided.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.3.3: Sensory Characteristics
checkpoints.requirement_text: Instructions provided for understanding and operating content do not rely solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, colour, size, visual location, orientation, or sound.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.3.3 (Sensory Characteristics) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: Many users including the visually challenged cannot perceive shape, size or use information about location or orientation. For such users the content that relies on knowledge of the shape or position of objects becomes inaccessible (for example, “round button” or “button to the right”).
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Provide additional information in content that relies solely on sensory characteristics of components such as shape, size, visual location, orientation, or sound. This can be done by providing textual identification of items that otherwise rely only on sensory information to be understood; for example, a round button is provided on a form to submit the form and move onto the next step. The button is labelled with the text “go.” The instructions state, “to submit the form press the round button labelled go”. This includes both shape and textual information to locate the button.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.3.4: Orientation
checkpoints.requirement_text: Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is essential.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.3.4 (Orientation) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit:
This Success Criterion requires content to display in the orientation preferred by the user and not restrict the orientation. This improves accessibility for users who rely on a specific orientation and promotes flexibility in technology design.
Users with dexterity impairments, who have a mounted device will be able to use the content in their fixed orientation.
Users with low vision will be able to view content in the orientation that works best for them, for example to increase the text size by viewing content in landscape.
guidelines_detail.developer_action:
Developers must ensure that content displays in the orientation (portrait or landscape) preferred by the user. Content does not restrict its view and operation to a single display orientation, such as portrait or landscape, unless a specific display orientation is essential. Examples of situations where a specific display orientation is essential could be a:
Banking app that requires the device to be in landscape mode to capture an image of a check easily and accurately for deposit; and
Piano app that requires the device to be in landscape mode to allow room for enough of the piano keys to be functionally usable. Since a piano app is emulating a physical piano keyboard that needs to retain relative physical characteristics between keys, either too few keys would be available, or the keys would be much too narrow.
guidelines_detail.evaluator_action: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

checkpoints.title: WCAG 2.1 1.3.5: Identify Input Purpose
checkpoints.requirement_text:
The purpose of each input field collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined when:
- The input field serves a purpose identified in the Input Purposes for User Interface Components section; and
- The content is implemented using technologies with support for identifying the expected meaning for form input data.
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Rendered/interactive conformance with WCAG 2.1 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose) on public pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Requires rendered visual, interactive, media, or multi-page semantic evaluation beyond static HTTP/HTML parsing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: The evaluator will test it manually and by using the Accessibility extension to browser/accessibility plug-in/web accessibility tool/assistive technology to check the conformity of this checkpoint.

guidelines_detail.benefit: People with language and memory related disabilities or disabilities that affects executive function and decision-making benefit from the browser auto-filling personal information (such as name or address) .People with learning disability can employ assistive technology which adds icons to input fields to communicate the purpose of the fields visually and people with motor impairments also benefit from reducing the need for manual input when filling out forms.
guidelines_detail.developer_action: Developers must ensure that the purpose of a form input collecting information about the user can be programmatically determined, so that user agents can extract and present this purpose to users using different modalities. Developers can use autofill attribute to programmatically link a pre-defined and published taxonomic term to the input, so that the inputs can also be machine-interpreted.
