checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: (2) The appropriate Government shall, within eighteen months from the commencement of this Act, compile in its official language a guide containing such information, in an easily comprehensible form and manner, as may reasonably be required by a person who wishes to exercise any right specified in this Act. (3) The appropriate Government shall, if necessary, update and publish the guidelines... include— (a) the objects of this Act; (b) the postal and street address, the phone and fax number and, if available, electronic mail address of the CPIO or SPIO of every public authority... (c) the manner and the form in which request... shall be made... (f) all remedies in law... (g) section 4... (h) notices regarding fees...
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Citizen Help & Official-Language Guidance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Nodal Appropriate Government portal publishes an official-language Citizen RTI Guide covering clauses (a)-(i) of Section 26(3).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Guide exists only in English (omitting official language) or is severely outdated (pre-2012 rules / dead addresses).
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Section 26(2)-(3) Citizen RTI Guide observed on an applicable Central/State Appropriate Government nodal portal.
benign_explanations: State-level guide may be hosted on the State Information Commission or State Administrative Reforms portal rather than the main State homepage.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.title: Prominent Homepage RTI / Proactive Disclosure Link and Visible Date of Last Update
checkpoints.requirement_text: Host a prominent RTI / Proactive Disclosure link directly reachable from the website homepage and display a visible 'Last Updated' / review date so citizens can judge disclosure freshness.
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 2 & Ch. 4
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Both a visible RTI link AND a valid Last Updated / Reviewed date string observed on landing/RTI pages.
checkpoints.caveats: Issued by DoPT for Central Ministries/Departments/Public Authorities and recommended to State Governments. Subject to RTI Section 24 exemptions.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Homepage prominently links to RTI/Proactive Disclosure and displays a concrete, recent Last Updated date. Partial/stale: Either RTI link or Last Updated date is absent, or the displayed date is >18 months old.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Public authorities are directed to publish suo motu disclosures under Section 4 in a structured, user-friendly, easily accessible manner on their official websites with regular updating and visible currency.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Quality Checkpoint 5 (Last Updated Date) & Mandatory RTI Link

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Homepage prominently links to RTI/Proactive Disclosure and displays a concrete, recent Last Updated date.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Either RTI link or Last Updated date is absent, or the displayed date is >18 months old.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Neither prominent RTI navigation nor a Last Updated date observed.
benign_explanations: Some portals display update timestamps only inside individual document tables rather than the homepage footer.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.title: Published Annual Third-Party RTI Transparency Audit Report
checkpoints.requirement_text: Central public authorities must undergo an annual third-party Transparency Audit of Section 4 suo motu disclosures and publish the audit report on their website.
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines on Suo Motu Disclosure & Annual Third-Party Transparency Audit · DoPT OM 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013) Paras 4.4–4.5; OM dated 07.11.2019; OM dated 20.09.2022
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Link or PDF mentioning 'Transparency Audit' / 'Third-Party Audit' of Section 4 disclosures on the RTI page.
checkpoints.caveats: Mandatory for Central Government Ministries, Departments, and Central Public Authorities overseen by CIC; optional/state-policy-dependent for State Government portals. Subject to RTI Section 24 exemptions.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Recent (last 1–2 years) Third-Party RTI Transparency Audit report hosted publicly on the authority's RTI section. Partial/stale: Only self-appraisal report published without independent third-party audit, or audit report is >2 years stale.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Every Ministry/Public Authority shall get its proactive disclosure package audited by a third party every year (through designated Government Training Institutes / peer public authorities under the 6-category CIC Transparency Audit proforma) and host the audit report on its website and submit it to CIC.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Content Guidelines — RTI / Transparency Audit Compliance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Recent (last 1–2 years) Third-Party RTI Transparency Audit report hosted publicly on the authority's RTI section.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Only self-appraisal report published without independent third-party audit, or audit report is >2 years stale.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Third-Party RTI Transparency Audit report observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: State/local public authorities are governed by State Information Commissions and may not be under the Central CIC transparency audit mandate.
Audit report may be filed on the CIC portal without a mirror link on a subdomain.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.serial_no: DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Procurement) & CIC Proforma Category 2
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of Tenders, Procurement Notices and Contract Awards
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish a discoverable Tenders / Procurement section (or direct link to CPPP/GeM/State e-Procurement listings) covering active tenders and awarded contract particulars.
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Procurement) & CIC Proforma Category 2
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible Tenders / Procurement navigation link on homepage or RTI section.
checkpoints.caveats: Many authorities publish tenders via CPPP (eprocure.gov.in), GeM (gem.gov.in), or State e-procurement portals; linking to those portals from a Tenders nav item satisfies discoverability.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Dedicated Tenders/Procurement page or link to official e-Procurement/CPPP/GeM tender listings with active/awarded records. Partial/stale: Tenders section exists but only displays notices from >2 years ago or omits contract award disclosures.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Public authorities should proactively place information relating to procurement — including tender notices, corrigenda, and details of contracts awarded — in the public domain.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Content Guidelines — Tenders & Procurement

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Dedicated Tenders/Procurement page or link to official e-Procurement/CPPP/GeM tender listings with active/awarded records.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Tenders section exists but only displays notices from >2 years ago or omits contract award disclosures.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Tenders or Procurement link observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: Subordinate/service subdomains may centralise all procurement on the parent department website or CPPP/GeM.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.serial_no: DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Foreign & Domestic Tours) & CIC Proforma Category 2
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of Foreign and Domestic Official Tours of Senior Officials
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish periodic statements of foreign and domestic official tours of Ministers/heads/senior officials with dates, destinations, and expenditure (or Nil statement).
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Foreign & Domestic Tours) & CIC Proforma Category 2
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Foreign/Domestic Tours link or table inside RTI Proactive Disclosure section.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies primarily to Central Ministries/Departments/Public Authorities; non-applicable or Nil for small offices with no foreign/official tours.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Published statement/table of foreign & domestic tours with dates, destinations, and expenditure (or explicit Nil report). Partial/stale: Lists tours without expenditure figures or latest tour statement is >2 years old.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Public authorities should proactively disclose details of foreign and domestic official tours undertaken by Ministers and senior officers (Joint Secretary and above / equivalent), including places visited, period, number of members, and total expenditure incurred.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW / CIC Transparency Audit Proforma — Category 2 (Budget & Programmes)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Published statement/table of foreign & domestic tours with dates, destinations, and expenditure (or explicit Nil report).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Lists tours without expenditure figures or latest tour statement is >2 years old.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No foreign/domestic official tour disclosure observed on RTI pages.
benign_explanations: Field/district offices or State units outside DoPT's Central mandate may not have foreign official travel.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of Public-Private Partnership (PPP) Projects and Concession Agreements
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish details of PPP projects, concession terms, outlays, and monitoring reports (or explicitly note 'Not Applicable / Nil' where no PPP projects exist).
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Public-Private Partnerships)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: PPP Projects / Concession Agreements entry in RTI proactive disclosure section.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies only where the public authority executes PPP projects; explicit 'Nil / Not Applicable' satisfies the item.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Lists active PPP projects, partner entities, outlays, and concession summaries — or explicitly states 'Nil / No PPP projects'. Partial/stale: Mentions PPP projects qualitatively without financial outlay or concession summaries.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: If a public authority implements projects through Public-Private Partnerships (PPP), details of concession agreements, private partners, financial outlays, and periodic performance reports should be disclosed proactively (subject to statutory commercial-confidence severability).
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: CIC Transparency Audit Proforma — Category 1/2 (PPP Disclosures)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Lists active PPP projects, partner entities, outlays, and concession summaries — or explicitly states 'Nil / No PPP projects'.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Mentions PPP projects qualitatively without financial outlay or concession summaries.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Neither PPP disclosures nor a 'Nil / N/A' declaration observed on RTI pages.
benign_explanations: Most non-infrastructure public authorities do not execute PPP projects.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.serial_no: DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Transfer Policy & Orders)
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of Transfer Policy and Transfer Orders
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish the authority's transfer/posting policy and official transfer orders in the public domain.
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (Transfer Policy & Orders)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Transfer Policy / Transfer Orders link inside RTI or Administration/Circulars section.
checkpoints.caveats: Single-location autonomous bodies or cadreless units without transferable posts may legitimately note 'Not Applicable'.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Published employee transfer policy and periodic transfer orders (or explicit 'N/A — single-station office' statement). Partial/stale: Transfer policy published without recent orders or policy is visibly superseded.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Public authorities should proactively place transfer policies and transfer orders on their websites to promote administrative transparency.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: CIC Transparency Audit Proforma — Category 4 (E-Governance / Transfer Policy)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Published employee transfer policy and periodic transfer orders (or explicit 'N/A — single-station office' statement).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Transfer policy published without recent orders or policy is visibly superseded.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No transfer policy or transfer orders disclosure observed.
benign_explanations: Personnel transfers may be managed centrally by a parent cadre-controlling ministry (e.g., DoPT / State GAD).

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.serial_no: DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (RTI Applications & Appeals) & CIC Proforma Category 4
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of PII-Redacted RTI Applications, First Appeals, Replies and FAQs
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish PII-redacted RTI applications, first appeals, and replies online (plus FAQs) so citizens can access already-disclosed answers without filing duplicate requests.
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (RTI Applications & Appeals) & CIC Proforma Category 4
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Links for RTI Replies / RTI Applications & Appeals Disposal / RTI FAQs under RTI section.
checkpoints.caveats: Personal information of RTI applicants MUST be excluded (RTI Sec 8(1)(j) as amended by DPDP Act 2023 w.e.f. 13-11-2025). If a portal leaks applicant PII (mobile/email/address), our auditor MUST NOT copy it.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Publishes PII-redacted RTI requests/appeals and replies (or substantive RTI FAQs) updated periodically. Partial/stale: Only general website FAQs exist, or RTI replies archive stopped >2 years ago.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: All Public Authorities shall proactively disclose RTI applications and appeals received and their responses on the website (excluding personal information of applicants under Section 8(1)(j)), along with Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) derived from recurring queries.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: CIC Transparency Audit Proforma — Category 4 (FAQs & RTI Replies)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Publishes PII-redacted RTI requests/appeals and replies (or substantive RTI FAQs) updated periodically.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Only general website FAQs exist, or RTI replies archive stopped >2 years ago.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No RTI replies/appeals disclosure or RTI FAQs observed.
benign_explanations: Authorities strictly redacting personal data under amended Sec 8(1)(j) may publish topic-wise FAQs instead of raw request logs.

checkpoints.section_name: DoPT / CIC · Suo Motu Disclosure & Audit Guidelines
checkpoints.serial_no: DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (CAG/PAC Paras & Grants) & CIC Proforma Category 5
checkpoints.title: Proactive Disclosure of CAG/PAC Audit Paragraphs, ATNs and Discretionary/Non-Discretionary Grants
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish tabled CAG/PAC audit observations and Action Taken Notes (ATNs), plus statements of discretionary and non-discretionary grants disbursed (or Nil statement).
checkpoints.citation: DoPT Guidelines for Implementation of Suo Motu Disclosure under Section 4 of the RTI Act, 2005 · DoPT OM No. 1/6/2011-IR (15.04.2013), Ch. 1 (CAG/PAC Paras & Grants) & CIC Proforma Category 5
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: CAG/PAC Audit Paras / ATN or Discretionary Grants disclosure link under RTI or Reports section.
checkpoints.caveats: CAG/PAC paras are disclosed only after being tabled in Parliament/State Legislature (respecting Section 8(1)(c) parliamentary privilege).
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Publishes tabled CAG/PAC audit summaries/ATNs and discretionary/non-discretionary grants (or explicit Nil statement). Partial/stale: Mentions audit paras or grants in heading only with broken links or >3-year-old records.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Public authorities should proactively disclose CAG and PAC audit paragraphs (along with Action Taken Notes once laid before Parliament/Legislature) and particulars of discretionary and non-discretionary grants allocated/disbursed.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: CIC Transparency Audit Proforma — Category 5 (Information as Prescribed)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Publishes tabled CAG/PAC audit summaries/ATNs and discretionary/non-discretionary grants (or explicit Nil statement).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Mentions audit paras or grants in heading only with broken links or >3-year-old records.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Neither CAG/PAC ATN nor discretionary grant disclosure observed.
benign_explanations: Authority may have no pending CAG/PAC paragraphs or grant-in-aid schemes; CAG reports are also hosted on cag.gov.in.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: RPwD Act 2016 Sec 40, 42(i), 46; RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(i)
checkpoints.title: Mandatory Website Accessibility Standard (GIGW), Screen Reader Access and Accessibility Statement
checkpoints.requirement_text: Every government establishment website must comply with GIGW accessibility standards and provide discoverable Screen Reader Access information / Accessibility Statement / Accessibility controls.
checkpoints.citation: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 · RPwD Act 2016 Sec 40, 42(i), 46; RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(i)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible link to Screen Reader Access / Accessibility Statement and/or Skip to Main Content anchor.
checkpoints.caveats: Binding statutory standard across all Government establishments (Central, State, UT, and Local) under RPwD Act Sec 40 & 46.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Visible Screen Reader Access and/or Accessibility Statement link present and reachable on homepage. Partial/stale: Only font-size +/- buttons appear without any Screen Reader Access guide or Accessibility Statement.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Rule 15(1) Every establishment shall comply with the following standards relating to physical environment, transport and information and communication technology, namely:— (c) Information and Communication Technology— (i) website standard as specified in the guidelines for Indian Government websites, as adopted by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances, Government of India;
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Accessibility Guidelines & Annexure II (Screen Reader Access / Accessibility Statement)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Visible Screen Reader Access and/or Accessibility Statement link present and reachable on homepage.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Only font-size +/- buttons appear without any Screen Reader Access guide or Accessibility Statement.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Screen Reader Access or Accessibility Statement link observed on landing page.
benign_explanations: A minimal API/redirect portal may rely on accessibility tools hosted on its parent portal.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: RPwD Act 2016 Sec 42(i); RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(ii)
checkpoints.title: Website Documents Published in Accessible ePUB or OCR-Based PDF Format
checkpoints.requirement_text: Public documents hosted on `.gov.in` websites must be published in accessible text-extractable (OCR-based/tagged) PDF or ePUB format rather than unsearchable image-only scans.
checkpoints.citation: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 & Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017 · RPwD Act 2016 Sec 42(i); RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(ii)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Detection of .pdf/.epub links on landing/RTI pages surfaces candidate public documents for bounded OCR/text-layer sampling by the agent.
checkpoints.caveats: Checking whether linked PDFs have a real text/OCR layer vs image-only scans requires downloading sampled PDFs (bounded) or agent inspection — do NOT assume from `.pdf` extension alone!
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Sampled public PDFs contain selectable/searchable text (OCR or digitally generated) or ePUB/HTML equivalents are provided. Partial/stale: Mix of digitally generated PDFs and unscanned image-only circulars/orders.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Rule 15(1)(c)(ii) documents to be placed on websites shall be in Electronic Publication (ePUB) or Optical Character Reader (OCR) based pdf format:
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Document Accessibility (PDF/ePUB & Accessible Content)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Sampled public PDFs contain selectable/searchable text (OCR or digitally generated) or ePUB/HTML equivalents are provided.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Mix of digitally generated PDFs and unscanned image-only circulars/orders.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Sampled public PDFs contain zero extractable text layer (pure scanned images) with no HTML/ePUB alternative.
benign_explanations: Legacy archival gazettes or signed historical orders predating 2017 may exist only as archival scans.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(iii) (inserted via G.S.R. 359(E), 10.05.2023) — BIS IS 17802 (Part 1: 2021 & Part 2: 2022)
checkpoints.title: BIS IS 17802 / WCAG 2.1 Level AA Automated HTML Accessibility Baseline
checkpoints.requirement_text: Websites must satisfy statutory IS 17802 / WCAG 2.1 Level AA accessibility criteria; deterministic HTML checks can verify baseline structural requirements (, descriptive , skip link, meaningful <img alt>, form <label>/aria-label, semantic landmarks).
checkpoints.citation: Rights of Persons with Disabilities · RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(iii) (inserted via G.S.R. 359(E), 10.05.2023) — BIS IS 17802 (Part 1: 2021 & Part 2: 2022)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: <html lang='...'> attribute present and valid (WCAG 3.1.1)
checkpoints.caveats: Automated HTML inspection covers only machine-checkable WCAG 2.1 AA / IS 17802 Part 1 structural indicators (approx. 30–40% of WCAG criteria); colour contrast, keyboard focus order, and screen-reader usability require browser/agent or human assistive-tech testing.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: All baseline HTML structural accessibility signals (<html lang>, <title>, skip link, img alt attribute coverage, labelled inputs, main landmark) observed. Partial/stale: Some structural indicators present (e.g., <title> and lang) while images lack alt attributes or skip link/form labels are missing.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Rule 15(1)(c)(iii) mandates conformance to Indian Standard IS 17802 (Information Technology — Accessibility Requirements for ICT Products and Services: Part 1: 2021 Requirements and Part 2: 2022 Determination of Conformance, aligned with WCAG 2.1 Level AA) for websites, mobile apps, and ICT-based public facilities and services.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA / IS 17802) — aligns with Annexure II accessibility matrix

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: All baseline HTML structural accessibility signals (<html lang>, <title>, skip link, img alt attribute coverage, labelled inputs, main landmark) observed.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Some structural indicators present (e.g., <title> and lang) while images lack alt attributes or skip link/form labels are missing.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Multiple core HTML accessibility attributes (<html lang>, img alt, skip link, landmarks) absent on sampled landing page.
benign_explanations: Client-side SPA frameworks may inject ARIA labels or landmarks via JavaScript after initial HTML load.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.title: Captions, Audio Description or Transcripts for Web Audio/Video Multimedia
checkpoints.requirement_text: Where a `.gov.in` page embeds audio or video multimedia, it should provide closed captions (<track kind='captions'>), transcripts, or audio descriptions.
checkpoints.citation: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 · RPwD Act 2016 Section 42(ii) & IS 17802 Part 1 (WCAG 1.2)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: If <video> or <audio> tags appear on sampled pages, check for child <track kind='captions'|'subtitles'> or nearby transcript link.
checkpoints.caveats: Applicable ONLY when the sampled website actually hosts or embeds <video>/<audio>/media players; mark not_applicable when no multimedia is present.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Embedded audio/video media includes <track> captions, transcripts, or sign-language/audio-description alternatives (or site has no multimedia). Partial/stale: Some embedded videos include captions/transcripts while others lack alternatives.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Section 42. The appropriate Government shall take measures to ensure that,— (ii) persons with disabilities have access to electronic media by providing audio description, sign language interpretation and close captioning;
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Accessibility — Time-Based Media (WCAG 1.2)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Embedded audio/video media includes <track> captions, transcripts, or sign-language/audio-description alternatives (or site has no multimedia).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Some embedded videos include captions/transcripts while others lack alternatives.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Hosted <video>/<audio> elements observed with no captions, <track>, or text transcript.
benign_explanations: Embedded YouTube/DD News players may provide captions inside the third-party iframe not visible in outer HTML.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(iii) — BIS IS 17802 (Part 2: 2022 Determination of Conformance)
checkpoints.title: Formal IS 17802 Part 2 Accessibility Conformance Evaluation and Governance
checkpoints.requirement_text: Public authorities must conduct full conformance testing (keyboard-only, screen readers, contrast, assistive tech) and maintain internal accessibility remediation governance.
checkpoints.citation: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Rules, 2017 · RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 15(1)(c)(iii) — BIS IS 17802 (Part 2: 2022 Determination of Conformance)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Optional public Accessibility Conformance / STQC badge.
checkpoints.caveats: End-to-end manual assistive technology conformance evaluation and internal QA records cannot be verified solely via static HTTP reads.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires formal IS 17802 Part 2 conformance test report or STQC accessibility audit record. Partial/stale: Not determinable from passive HTTP/HTML alone.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: IS 17802 (Part 2): 2022 specifies formal determination of conformance and assistive-technology testing methodologies for ICT products and services.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Accessibility Testing & STQC CQW Certification

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires formal IS 17802 Part 2 conformance test report or STQC accessibility audit record.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from passive HTTP/HTML alone.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: Internal accessibility test reports may be maintained by NIC/agency teams without public posting.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: Official Languages Act, 1963 Section 3(3); Dept. of Official Language (rajbhasha.gov.in) Bilingual Website Guidelines
checkpoints.title: Bilingual Hindi and English Availability on Union / Central Government Websites
checkpoints.requirement_text: Union/Central Government ministries, departments, offices, and Union PSUs must provide their websites bilingually in both Hindi and English (while State/UT portals follow their respective State official language norms alongside English).
checkpoints.citation: The Official Languages Act, 1963 · Official Languages Act, 1963 Section 3(3); Dept. of Official Language (rajbhasha.gov.in) Bilingual Website Guidelines
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible Hindi toggle/link ('हिन्दी' / 'हिंदी' / '/hi/') OR Devanagari Hindi content present alongside English on Central `.gov.in` portals.
checkpoints.caveats: CRITICAL JURISDICTION GUARD: The Official Languages Act, 1963 applies to the UNION (Central Government ministries, departments, attached offices, and Union PSUs). State/UT portals (e.g., *.tn.gov.in, *.kerala.gov.in, *.karnataka.gov.in, *.wb.gov.in, *.maharashtra.gov.in) are governed by their respective State Official Languages Acts — NEVER flag a non-Hindi State portal for lacking Hindi!
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Central Government `.gov.in` website provides both English and Hindi navigation/versions. Partial/stale: Hindi link is present in header but leads to a 404, placeholder page, or untranslated English text.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Section 3(3) mandates that both Hindi and English shall be used for resolutions, general orders, rules, notifications, administrative/other reports, press communiqués, papers laid before Parliament, contracts, agreements, licences, permits, tender notices, and tender forms issued by the Central Government.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Multilingual / Bilingual Website Compliance (Hindi & English)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Central Government `.gov.in` website provides both English and Hindi navigation/versions.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Hindi link is present in header but leads to a 404, placeholder page, or untranslated English text.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Hindi version link or Devanagari bilingual indicator observed on a Central Government `.gov.in` landing page.
benign_explanations: Portal may belong to a State/UT government outside the Union Official Languages Act scope.
Bilingual toggle may be rendered dynamically via JavaScript or hosted on a separate Hindi subdomain.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: Official Languages Act, 1963 Section 3(3)(i)-(iii); Official Languages Rules, 1976 Rule 6
checkpoints.title: Bilingual Issuance of Statutory Notifications, General Orders, Reports, Press Releases and Tenders
checkpoints.requirement_text: Central Government portals publishing notifications, general orders, administrative reports, press releases, and tender notices must publish them bilingually in Hindi and English.
checkpoints.citation: The Official Languages Act, 1963 & Official Languages · Official Languages Act, 1963 Section 3(3)(i)-(iii); Official Languages Rules, 1976 Rule 6
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Parallel Hindi & English document links or diglot PDFs in Notifications/Orders/Reports/Tenders sections.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies strictly to Central Government ministries, departments, offices, and Union corporations/PSUs — NOT State Government portals.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Sampled Central Government notifications, reports, press releases, and tenders are available in both Hindi and English (or diglot PDFs). Partial/stale: Website chrome is bilingual, but linked notifications/tenders/reports are uploaded in English only.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 (and Rule 6 of the Official Languages Rules, 1976), resolutions, general orders, rules, notifications, administrative reports, press releases, parliamentary papers, contracts, licences, permits, and tender notices/forms of Central Government offices shall invariably be issued in both Hindi and English.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Multilingual Content Parity Guidelines

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Sampled Central Government notifications, reports, press releases, and tenders are available in both Hindi and English (or diglot PDFs).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Website chrome is bilingual, but linked notifications/tenders/reports are uploaded in English only.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Only English statutory documents observed on an applicable Central Government portal.
benign_explanations: Hindi versions may be published on the Hindi mirror (`/hi/`) rather than side-by-side on the English page.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.title: Diglot / Bilingual Hindi-English Manuals, Codes, Procedural Literature and Forms
checkpoints.requirement_text: Central Government manuals, codes, procedural literature, and downloadable citizen/official forms published on Union portals should be available bilingually in Hindi and English.
checkpoints.citation: Official Languages · Official Languages Rules, 1976 Rule 11(1) & Rule 11(2)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Bilingual/diglot manuals and downloadable forms in Forms/Manuals section of Central portals.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies to Central Government offices (subject to Central Government exemption proviso under Rule 11(3)). Not applicable to State Government portals.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Procedural manuals and citizen forms on Central Government portal are provided in Hindi and English (diglot or parallel versions). Partial/stale: Some major forms are bilingual while procedural manuals are English-only.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Rule 11(1) All manuals, codes and other procedural literature relating to Central Government offices shall be printed or cyclostyled, as the case may be, and published both in Hindi and English in diglot form. (2) The forms and headings of registers used in any Central Government office shall be in Hindi and in English.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Multilingual Forms & Documents

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Procedural manuals and citizen forms on Central Government portal are provided in Hindi and English (diglot or parallel versions).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Some major forms are bilingual while procedural manuals are English-only.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Only English-language manuals and forms observed on an applicable Central Government portal.
benign_explanations: Central Government may have exempted specific technical/scientific offices under Rule 11 proviso.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: State Emblem Act, 2005 Section 2(b) & Schedule; Rules, 2007 (G.S.R. 643(E)) & MHA Advisories
checkpoints.title: Complete Display of State Emblem of India Including Devanagari Motto 'सत्यमेव जयते'
checkpoints.requirement_text: Where an entitled `.gov.in` website displays the State Emblem of India, the emblem must be complete with the Devanagari motto 'सत्यमेव जयते' (Satyameva Jayate) inscribed below the abacus — never an incomplete lion-capital graphic omitting the motto.
checkpoints.citation: The State Emblem of India · State Emblem Act, 2005 Section 2(b) & Schedule; Rules, 2007 (G.S.R. 643(E)) & MHA Advisories
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator:
tags in
whose src/alt/title references 'emblem', 'ashoka', 'satyamev', or 'lion' (surfaces emblem image URL for visual/agent verification of the Devanagari motto).
checkpoints.caveats: Applies ONLY when the website displays the State Emblem of India (State governments using a distinct State seal or autonomous/PSU bodies not authorised to display the State Emblem under Rules 2007 Schedule I/II are NOT required to display it — and indeed Rule 10 restricts unauthorised use!). Visual verification of whether the Devanagari motto appears inside the logo image requires agent/vision inspection.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Displayed State Emblem of India clearly includes the Devanagari motto 'सत्यमेव जयते' below the abacus (or portal lawfully uses an institutional/state seal instead). Partial/stale: Emblem is rendered at tiny/blurry resolution where the motto is illegible or distorted.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Under Section 2(b) and the Schedule of the State Emblem of India (Prohibition of Improper Use) Act, 2005 and the State Emblem of India (Regulation of Use) Rules, 2007, the national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (सत्यमेव जयते) inscribed in Devanagari script below the profile of the Lion Capital forms an integral constituent part of the State Emblem of India.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Visual Identity — Official Emblem & Government Ownership Display

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Displayed State Emblem of India clearly includes the Devanagari motto 'सत्यमेव जयते' below the abacus (or portal lawfully uses an institutional/state seal instead).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Emblem is rendered at tiny/blurry resolution where the motto is illegible or distorted.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: State Emblem of India graphic is displayed WITHOUT the mandatory Devanagari motto 'सत्यमेव जयते' below the abacus.
benign_explanations: Autonomous bodies, PSUs, and certain State entities are restricted under Rules 2007 from displaying the National State Emblem and properly display their own logo.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: State Emblem Act, 2005 Sections 3 & 4; Rules, 2007 Rules 4 & 10(3)
checkpoints.title: Authorised Governmental Use of State Emblem Without Commercial Misuse
checkpoints.requirement_text: Only authorised Constitutional/Union/State authorities may display the State Emblem (and States incorporating it in a modified emblem require Central Government approval under Rule 4); commercial or private trade endorsements alongside the emblem are prohibited.
checkpoints.citation: The State Emblem of India · State Emblem Act, 2005 Sections 3 & 4; Rules, 2007 Rules 4 & 10(3)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Internal MHA authorisation / Schedule entitlement cannot be verified from public HTML.
checkpoints.caveats: Determining whether a specific registered society, corporation, or modified state seal holds Central Government authorisation requires internal MHA approval records.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires verifying entity entitlement under Schedule I/II of the 2007 Rules or MHA written permission. Partial/stale: Not determinable from passive HTML reads.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Section 3 prohibits improper use of the emblem creating a false impression of government authority without Central Government permission; Section 4 prohibits use for trade, business, calling, or profession; Rule 4 & Rule 10 govern State adoption and restrictions on bodies/associations.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Visual Identity & Ownership Attribution

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires verifying entity entitlement under Schedule I/II of the 2007 Rules or MHA written permission.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from passive HTML reads.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: Many bodies on `.gov.in` hold statutory or MHA approvals not published on their homepage.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: NIC .gov.in Domain Registration Policy; CERT-In / GIGW Site-Wide HTTPS/TLS Mandate
checkpoints.title: Valid Site-Wide HTTPS / TLS Transport on Official .gov.in Hostname
checkpoints.requirement_text: Every citizen-facing `.gov.in` hostname must serve valid HTTPS over a trusted certificate chain without redirecting back to plaintext `http://`.
checkpoints.citation: NIC .gov.in Domain Registration Policy · NIC .gov.in Domain Registration Policy; CERT-In / GIGW Site-Wide HTTPS/TLS Mandate
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Successful verified HTTPS GET on assigned `.gov.in` hostname (valid CA chain, valid SNI, no TLS handshake error, no redirect downgrading to http://).
checkpoints.caveats: Strictly passive TLS handshake verification via standard HTTPS GET (already enforced by `gov_pages.py` which verifies TLS + SNI on DNS-pinned public IP). Never probe ports or run active SSL scanners.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Assigned `.gov.in` hostname completes verified HTTPS connection cleanly and stays on HTTPS. Partial/stale: HTTPS works on `www.<domain>` only while apex redirects to plaintext `http://`, or intermediate chain issues occur.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Government websites hosted under the exclusive .gov.in namespace administered by NIC must implement site-wide HTTPS with valid TLS certificates (TLS 1.2+, strong SHA-256/2048-bit+ keys) and avoid downgrading visitors to plaintext HTTP.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security & Hosting Guidelines — Mandatory HTTPS/TLS

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Assigned `.gov.in` hostname completes verified HTTPS connection cleanly and stays on HTTPS.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: HTTPS works on `www.<domain>` only while apex redirects to plaintext `http://`, or intermediate chain issues occur.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: HTTPS handshake fails due to expired/mismatched/untrusted certificate or forces plaintext HTTP downgrade.
benign_explanations: Host may be decommissioned, internal-only, or experiencing temporary maintenance/firewall filtering.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: E-mail Policy of Government of India (2015), Core Mandate & NIC Implementing Agency Clauses
checkpoints.title: Official Government Email Domains (@gov.in / @nic.in) Used Instead of Commercial Webmail
checkpoints.requirement_text: Public contact emails displayed on `.gov.in` websites (Contact Us / RTI / Grievance pages) should use official government domains (`@gov.in`, `@nic.in`, or institutional `.ac.in`/`.edu.in`/`.org.in` for autonomous bodies) rather than personal/commercial webmail (`@gmail.com`, `@yahoo.com`, `@rediffmail.com`, `@hotmail.com`).
checkpoints.citation: E-mail Policy of Government of India · E-mail Policy of Government of India (2015), Core Mandate & NIC Implementing Agency Clauses
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Emit TWO strictly boolean/categorical indicators: `official_gov_email_domain` (observed/not_observed) and `commercial_webmail_indicator` (observed/not_observed), supporting both `@` and `[at]/[dot]` obfuscation.
checkpoints.caveats: Supports NIC standard obfuscation (`[at]` / `[dot]` / `(at)` / `(dot)`). Autonomous academic/research institutions on `.gov.in` may lawfully use institutional `.ac.in`/`.edu.in`/`.res.in` mail domains; flag ONLY commercial consumer webmail domains (`gmail.com`, `yahoo.com`, `yahoo.co.in`, `rediffmail.com`, `hotmail.com`, `outlook.com`, `live.com`) as a neutral observation indicator.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Published contact email indicator(s) on landing/contact pages use official `@gov.in` / `@nic.in` (or approved institutional) domain with no commercial webmail observed. Partial/stale: Site lists both official `@gov.in`/`@nic.in` addresses and a commercial webmail address (e.g., `@gmail.com`) for a local office/cell.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Official communications across Central and participating State/UT Government organisations must exclusively use official government email services administered via NIC (@gov.in / @nic.in or approved institutional domains) rather than external commercial webmail providers (e.g., Gmail, Yahoo).
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Quality Checkpoint 10 (Contact Details) & MeitY Email Policy Compliance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Published contact email indicator(s) on landing/contact pages use official `@gov.in` / `@nic.in` (or approved institutional) domain with no commercial webmail observed.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Site lists both official `@gov.in`/`@nic.in` addresses and a commercial webmail address (e.g., `@gmail.com`) for a local office/cell.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Only commercial webmail indicator observed (or no email indicator observed at all).
benign_explanations: Small local offices, societies, or transitional portals sometimes list a legacy or field-unit commercial email alongside NIC migration.
Email may be rendered inside an anti-spam image rather than text.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: CERT-In & NIC-CERT Secure Website Guidelines; GIGW 3.0 Security Headers & Mixed Content
checkpoints.title: Passive HTTP Security Headers (HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Framing) and No Mixed Content
checkpoints.requirement_text: Passively inspect HTTP response headers on the sampled HTTPS page for `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options` (or CSP `frame-ancestors`), and `Referrer-Policy`, plus scan HTML `
checkpoints.citation: CERT-In / NIC-CERT / GIGW 3.0 Web Application Security Guidelines · CERT-In & NIC-CERT Secure Website Guidelines; GIGW 3.0 Security Headers & Mixed Content
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: HTTP response header `strict-transport-security` present with max-age > 0
checkpoints.caveats: STRICTLY PASSIVE READ-ONLY CHECK: Reads only response headers and HTML attributes already received from the normal GET request. Zero active probing, zero vulnerability scanning, zero payload injection!
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Baseline security headers (HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, CSP) observed in HTTP response and zero plaintext `http://` embedded subresources found in sampled HTML. Partial/stale: Some headers (e.g., X-Frame-Options / nosniff) present while HSTS or CSP is absent, or passive `http://` image links remain.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Government websites must enforce HTTPS with HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS), Content Security Policy (CSP) / clickjacking framing controls, MIME-sniffing protection (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`), and avoid loading active/passive subresources over insecure plaintext `http://`.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security Guidelines & CERT-In Web Hardening Baseline

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Baseline security headers (HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, CSP) observed in HTTP response and zero plaintext `http://` embedded subresources found in sampled HTML.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Some headers (e.g., X-Frame-Options / nosniff) present while HSTS or CSP is absent, or passive `http://` image links remain.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Baseline HTTP security headers absent in response or active `http://` script/stylesheet mixed content observed.
benign_explanations: Reverse proxies/CDNs or legacy NIC hosting templates may apply headers selectively or omit CSP for older CMS widgets.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: CERT-In / NIC-CERT HTTP Header Hardening (Server Banner & Technology Fingerprinting Suppression)
checkpoints.title: Suppression of Verbose Server / Framework Version Disclosure in HTTP Headers
checkpoints.requirement_text: Passively observe whether standard HTTP response headers expose exact version numbers (e.g., `Apache/2.4.x`, `PHP/7.x`, `ASP.NET 4.x`) via `Server`, `X-Powered-By`, or `X-AspNet-Version`.
checkpoints.citation: CERT-In / NIC-CERT Web Application Security Hardening Guidelines · CERT-In / NIC-CERT HTTP Header Hardening (Server Banner & Technology Fingerprinting Suppression)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Check `server`, `x-powered-by`, `x-aspnet-version`, `x-aspnetmvc-version` headers for explicit software version numbers (e.g., `/\d+\.\d+`).
checkpoints.caveats: Strictly passive inspection of headers returned by normal GET. NEVER publish raw vulnerable version strings in public findings (avoid aiding exploitation!); publish ONLY a neutral boolean indicator (`no_verbose_server_banner`: observed / not_observed).
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Response headers suppress exact web-server and framework version numbers. Partial/stale: Server header is clean, but `X-Powered-By` exposes runtime/CMS technology.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Web applications and servers should obscure verbose HTTP response headers (such as exact server software versions in `Server`, `X-Powered-By`, or `X-AspNet-Version`) to avoid disclosing implementation versions.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security & Hosting Hardening

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Response headers suppress exact web-server and framework version numbers.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Server header is clean, but `X-Powered-By` exposes runtime/CMS technology.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Verbose software/framework version strings observed in HTTP response headers (record boolean flag only, never raw banner).
benign_explanations: Shared NIC/State Data Centre infrastructure headers are often configured centrally at the load balancer.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: CERT-In Empanelled Security Audit Mandate & GIGW Security Clearance ('Safe to Host')
checkpoints.title: Pre-Hosting and Periodic CERT-In Empanelled Web Security Audit ('Safe to Host')
checkpoints.requirement_text: Public authorities must obtain and renew 'Safe to Host' security audit clearance from a CERT-In empanelled auditor before production deployment and periodically thereafter.
checkpoints.citation: MeitY / CERT-In / NIC Website Hosting & Pre-Hosting Security Audit Mandate · CERT-In Empanelled Security Audit Mandate & GIGW Security Clearance ('Safe to Host')
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Internal hosting compliance record (occasionally mentioned in footer or About/Audit page).
checkpoints.caveats: Security audit certificates are submitted internally to NIC/hosting centres and are typically NOT required to be published publicly on the homepage.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires internal 'Safe to Host' audit certificate from CERT-In empanelled auditor / NIC hosting records. Partial/stale: Not determinable from public HTML.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: All government websites, portals, and web applications must undergo a comprehensive Vulnerability Assessment and Penetration Testing (VAPT) security audit by a CERT-In empanelled auditing organisation (or NIC/STQC) prior to hosting and periodically / after major code changes.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security Guidelines — Security Audit Clearance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires internal 'Safe to Host' audit certificate from CERT-In empanelled auditor / NIC hosting records.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from public HTML.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: Government agencies routinely keep security audit certificates internal for operational security.

checkpoints.serial_no: IT Act, 2000 Section 70B(6); CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In dated 28.04.2022 (effective 27.06.2022)
checkpoints.title: CERT-In 2022 Directions (6-Hour Incident Reporting, 180-Day Indian Log Retention, NIC/NPL NTP Sync, CISO/PoC)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Government ICT operators and hosting agencies must maintain 180-day logs in India, synchronise clocks to NIC/NPL NTP, report cyber incidents within 6 hours, and register a PoC with CERT-In.
checkpoints.citation: CERT-In Cyber Security Directions dated 28.04.2022 under Section 70B · IT Act, 2000 Section 70B(6); CERT-In Directions No. 20(3)/2022-CERT-In dated 28.04.2022 (effective 27.06.2022)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Backend infrastructure and SOC compliance only; not publicly observable.
checkpoints.caveats: Strictly backend infrastructure & SOC compliance; completely unobservable from public HTTP/HTML.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires internal infrastructure, SOC, and CERT-In PoC filing records. Partial/stale: Not determinable from public web pages.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Directions under Section 70B(6) of the IT Act, 2000 mandate: 6-hour cyber incident reporting to CERT-In across 20 incident categories, 180-day rolling ICT log retention within Indian jurisdiction, system clock synchronisation with NIC/NPL NTP servers, and designating a Point of Contact (PoC/CISO).
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security Monitoring & Incident Response

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires internal infrastructure, SOC, and CERT-In PoC filing records.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from public web pages.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: Operated internally by NIC/State Data Centres and departmental CISOs.

checkpoints.serial_no: STQC Directorate (MeitY) Website Quality Certification Scheme (GIGW Conformity Mark)
checkpoints.title: STQC Certified Quality Website (CQW) / GIGW Conformity Badge Disclosure
checkpoints.requirement_text: Observe whether the website displays an official STQC Certified Quality Website (CQW) / GIGW conformity mark or certification reference (typically in the footer).
checkpoints.citation: STQC Website Quality Certification Scheme · STQC Directorate (MeitY) Website Quality Certification Scheme (GIGW Conformity Mark)
