checkpoints.caveats: STQC CQW certification is a formal third-party conformity mark; absence of a footer badge is a neutral observation (certification may be in progress or portal may be a small subdomain).
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: STQC Certified Quality Website (CQW) mark or valid STQC GIGW certification reference observed. Partial/stale: Displays an expired STQC badge or broken certificate verification link.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: The Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification (STQC) Directorate operates the Website Quality Certification Scheme awarding the Certified Quality Website (CQW) mark upon independent verification of GIGW quality, accessibility, and security compliance.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Conformity Assessment & STQC Website Quality Certification

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: STQC Certified Quality Website (CQW) mark or valid STQC GIGW certification reference observed.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Displays an expired STQC badge or broken certificate verification link.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No STQC CQW certification badge or reference observed on sampled landing page.
benign_explanations: Many legitimate `.gov.in` portals comply with GIGW internally or are undergoing recertification without displaying an STQC badge.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: DARPG Citizen's Charter Mandate (darpg.gov.in / goicharters.nic.in) — 6 Core Charter Components
checkpoints.title: Published Citizen's Charter (Vision, Services, Standards, Timelines & Grievance Redressal)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish an accessible Citizen's Charter link on the website containing concrete service delivery standards, timelines, and grievance channels.
checkpoints.citation: DARPG Citizen's Charter Guidelines · DARPG Citizen's Charter Mandate (darpg.gov.in / goicharters.nic.in) — 6 Core Charter Components
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible navigation/footer link to Citizen's Charter (or Client's Charter / Sevottam) on homepage or About/RTI section.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies to public authorities with citizen/public interface; internal backend tools or narrow service subdomains may link to the parent department's Citizen's Charter.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Accessible Citizen's Charter link present AND (upon agent inspection) covers vision/mission, services, delivery timelines, and grievance redressal. Partial/stale: Citizen's Charter link exists but document is >3 years outdated or omits concrete service delivery timelines.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: DARPG guidelines require Central and State government organisations with public interface to formulate, publish, and periodically review a Citizen's Charter incorporating: (1) Vision & Mission, (2) Business/services transacted, (3) Client groups, (4) Service standards & delivery timelines, (5) Grievance redressal mechanism, and (6) Expectations from clients.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Content Guidelines — Citizen's Charter & RTI Section 4(1)(b)(iv)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Accessible Citizen's Charter link present AND (upon agent inspection) covers vision/mission, services, delivery timelines, and grievance redressal.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Citizen's Charter link exists but document is >3 years outdated or omits concrete service delivery timelines.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Citizen's Charter link observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: Subordinate/technical subdomains often rely on the parent ministry/department's Citizen's Charter.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: DARPG Comprehensive Public Grievance Redressal Guidelines — CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in)
checkpoints.title: Public Grievance Redressal Mechanism and CPGRAMS / Official State Grievance Portal Link
checkpoints.requirement_text: Provide a prominent Public Grievances / Lodge Grievance link connecting citizens to CPGRAMS (`pgportal.gov.in`), the official State grievance portal (e.g., `jansunwai`, `cmhelpline`, `sampark`, `aaplesarkar`), or the authority's online grievance redressal module.
checkpoints.citation: DARPG Guidelines for Handling Public Grievances & CPGRAMS Mandate · DARPG Comprehensive Public Grievance Redressal Guidelines — CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Outbound link to `pgportal.gov.in` (CPGRAMS) OR visible Public Grievance / Grievance Redressal link on homepage/footer/contact page.
checkpoints.caveats: Union portals should link to `pgportal.gov.in` (CPGRAMS); State/UT portals may link to their official State Public Grievance Portal or CPGRAMS.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Prominent link to CPGRAMS (`pgportal.gov.in`), official State grievance portal, or authority public grievance redressal page observed. Partial/stale: Grievance link exists but points to a broken URL or static page with no online lodging channel.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: DARPG mandates a 24x7 web-enabled public grievance redressal channel via the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS at pgportal.gov.in) for Union bodies and integrated/official State grievance portals for State authorities.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Citizen Engagement — Public Grievance Redressal & CPGRAMS

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Prominent link to CPGRAMS (`pgportal.gov.in`), official State grievance portal, or authority public grievance redressal page observed.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Grievance link exists but points to a broken URL or static page with no online lodging channel.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Public Grievance / CPGRAMS link observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: Narrow technical/internal-utility subdomains may defer citizen grievances to the parent department portal.

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: DARPG Public Grievance Guidelines — Designation & Publication of Nodal Public Grievance Officer (PGO)
checkpoints.title: Published Designation and Official Contact Channel of Public Grievance Officer (PGO)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish the designation and official contact details of the Nodal Public Grievance Officer (PGO) on the Grievance Redressal or Contact Us page.
checkpoints.citation: DARPG Guidelines for Handling Public Grievances · DARPG Public Grievance Guidelines — Designation & Publication of Nodal Public Grievance Officer (PGO)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible mention of Public Grievance Officer / Grievance Redressal Officer / Nodal Officer for Public Grievances on Grievance or Contact page.
checkpoints.caveats: Record ONLY boolean presence of PGO designation — never copy personal phone/email values.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Public Grievance Officer / Nodal Grievance Officer designation and official contact channel observed. Partial/stale: Mentions grievance officer role generically without official office contact channel.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Ministries, departments, and public authorities are required to appoint a Nodal Officer for Public Grievances (Public Grievance Officer / PGO) of appropriate rank and publish their particulars for citizen accessibility.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Quality Checkpoint 10 (Contact Us — Public Grievance Officer)

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Public Grievance Officer / Nodal Grievance Officer designation and official contact channel observed.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Mentions grievance officer role generically without official office contact channel.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Public Grievance Officer designation observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: PGO listing may appear on the parent ministry portal or inside the CPGRAMS directory (`pgportal.gov.in`).

checkpoints.section_name: RPwD Act, Official Languages, State Emblem & DARPG
checkpoints.serial_no: DARPG / NIC GIGW 3.0 Governance Mandate — Web Information Manager (WIM)
checkpoints.title: Published Web Information Manager (WIM) Designation and Official Contact Details
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish a dedicated Web Information Manager (WIM) entry (on the homepage footer, Contact Us page, or WIM page) identifying the responsible officer designation and official government contact channel.
checkpoints.citation: DARPG / NIC Guidelines for Indian Government Websites and Apps · DARPG / NIC GIGW 3.0 Governance Mandate — Web Information Manager (WIM)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible 'Web Information Manager' link or section on homepage footer or Contact Us page.
checkpoints.caveats: Record ONLY boolean presence of Web Information Manager listing — never copy personal phone/email values.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Web Information Manager designation and official contact channel observed on homepage footer, WIM page, or Contact Us page. Partial/stale: Footer mentions 'Web Information Manager' text without linking to or stating the responsible officer's designation/contact.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Every Indian government website must designate a Web Information Manager (WIM) responsible for content quality, authenticity, timely updating, feedback handling, and GIGW compliance, and publish the WIM's details on the Contact Us / Web Information Manager page.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Quality Checkpoint 10 & Governance — Mandatory Web Information Manager

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Web Information Manager designation and official contact channel observed on homepage footer, WIM page, or Contact Us page.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Footer mentions 'Web Information Manager' text without linking to or stating the responsible officer's designation/contact.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Web Information Manager link or mention observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: On shared S3WaaS/State portals, the WIM may be listed inside a district/department Contact Us subpage.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: IT Act SPDI Rules 2011 Rule 4; GIGW Website Policies; DPDP Act 2023 Sec 5 & DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 3 (full enforcement 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.title: Published Privacy Policy / Citizen Data Collection Statement
checkpoints.requirement_text: Publish a clearly linked Privacy Policy (or Website Policies covering Privacy Policy) in the website footer/navigation explaining whether and how citizen personal data is collected, used, and protected.
checkpoints.conformance_level: Statutory Privacy Mandate (IT Act / DPDP Act 2023)
checkpoints.citation: Information Technology Act, 2000 · IT Act SPDI Rules 2011 Rule 4; GIGW Website Policies; DPDP Act 2023 Sec 5 & DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 3 (full enforcement 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Visible footer/nav link matching 'Privacy Policy' / 'Website Policies' / 'गोपनीयता नीति' on landing page.
checkpoints.caveats: LEGAL TIMELINE NOTE: Under Gazette Notifications G.S.R. 843(E) & G.S.R. 846(E) dated 13 November 2025, the DPDP Board and RTI Sec 8(1)(j) amendment took effect on 13.11.2025, Consent Managers on 13.11.2026, and substantive Data Fiduciary obligations (Sections 5–17 & Rules 3–16) reach full enforcement on 13 May 2027. Meanwhile GIGW Website Policies already require a Privacy Policy link on all `.gov.in` sites. Frame DPDP readiness neutrally.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Dedicated Privacy Policy (or Website Policies page including Privacy Policy) clearly linked from landing page. Partial/stale: Links to a combined Website Policies page containing only a generic 2-line boilerplate despite collecting extensive citizen PII via forms.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: SPDI Rules 2011 Rule 4 (and GIGW mandatory Website Policies) require publishing a clear, easily accessible Privacy Policy detailing personal information collected, purpose of collection/use, disclosure practices, and security safeguards; DPDP Act 2023 Section 5 & DPDP Rules 2025 Rule 3 (entering full enforcement on 13 May 2027) mandate plain-language itemised personal data notices.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Website Policies — Mandatory Privacy Policy

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Dedicated Privacy Policy (or Website Policies page including Privacy Policy) clearly linked from landing page.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Links to a combined Website Policies page containing only a generic 2-line boilerplate despite collecting extensive citizen PII via forms.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No Privacy Policy or Website Policies link observed on landing page.
benign_explanations: Static informational portals that collect zero personal data may include privacy terms inside a unified 'Website Policies' or 'Terms of Use' page.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: DPDP Act, 2023 Sections 5, 6, 7(b)-(d), 17(2)&(4); DPDP Rules, 2025 Rule 3 (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.title: Itemised Plain-Language Data Collection Notice on Citizen-Facing Forms (DPDP Readiness)
checkpoints.requirement_text: On `.gov.in` portals hosting citizen data-collection forms (registrations, grievances, scheme applications, feedback), inspect whether a plain-language notice explains what personal data is collected, the lawful purpose, and redressal options — accounting accurately for State Section 7(b)-(d) legitimate uses and the 13 May 2027 DPDP enforcement timeline.
checkpoints.conformance_level: Statutory Privacy Mandate (IT Act / DPDP Act 2023)
checkpoints.citation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 · DPDP Act, 2023 Sections 5, 6, 7(b)-(d), 17(2)&(4); DPDP Rules, 2025 Rule 3 (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Presence of citizen <form> inputs (excluding simple search bars) alongside Privacy Policy / data-collection notice text.
checkpoints.caveats: CRITICAL LEGAL NUANCES: (1) Applies ONLY to portals with citizen personal-data forms; static read-only sites are not_applicable. (2) State & its instrumentalities may process data without fresh consent under Section 7(b)-(d) for subsidies/benefits/services/certificates/statutory duties, and notified security agencies are exempt under Section 17(2)(a). (3) Full statutory enforcement of Section 5 / Rule 3 begins 13 May 2027 — frame observations as transparency / DPDP-readiness indicators, NEVER as legal violations.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Privacy policy / form notice clearly itemises data fields collected, purpose, retention/sharing practices, and citizen redressal pathway. Partial/stale: Generic GIGW boilerplate privacy policy exists ('we do not capture personal info unless you provide it') without itemising actual form data purposes.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Section 5 mandates an itemised plain-language notice detailing personal data collected, processing purposes, how Data Principals may exercise rights/withdraw consent, and how to complain to the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI). Section 7(b)-(d) provides specific legitimate uses for State subsidies, benefits, services, certificates, licences, and statutory functions subject to Rule standards, and Section 17(2)(a) provides notified State-security exemptions.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Privacy Policy & Citizen Data Forms

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Privacy policy / form notice clearly itemises data fields collected, purpose, retention/sharing practices, and citizen redressal pathway.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Generic GIGW boilerplate privacy policy exists ('we do not capture personal info unless you provide it') without itemising actual form data purposes.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Citizen data-collection form observed with no visible privacy/data-processing notice.
benign_explanations: DPDP Act Section 5 / Rule 3 reaches full statutory enforcement on 13 May 2027; State portals operating under Section 7(b)-(d) follow phased MeitY/NIC rollout.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: SPDI Rules 2011 Rule 5(9); DPDP Act 2023 Section 8(10) & Section 13 (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.title: Published Data Privacy Grievance Redressal / Grievance Officer / DPO Contact Channel
checkpoints.requirement_text: Portals collecting citizen personal data should publish the designation and official contact channel of a Data Protection Officer (DPO) or Grievance Officer within their Privacy Policy / Grievance page.
checkpoints.conformance_level: Statutory Privacy Mandate (IT Act / DPDP Act 2023)
checkpoints.citation: IT Act SPDI Rules, 2011 · SPDI Rules 2011 Rule 5(9); DPDP Act 2023 Section 8(10) & Section 13 (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Presence of Grievance Officer / DPO / Web Information Manager contact channel inside Privacy Policy page.
checkpoints.caveats: DPO appointment is statutorily mandatory only for notified Significant Data Fiduciaries (Sec 10); other Data Fiduciaries must publish a contact person/grievance mechanism (Sec 8(9)-(10), enforceable 13.05.2027).
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Privacy Policy or Grievance page specifies a designated Grievance Officer / DPO / official contact channel for data-protection queries. Partial/stale: Privacy Policy exists but provides no grievance contact or points only to a generic 'Contact Us' without redressal process.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Data Fiduciaries must publish business contact information of a Data Protection Officer (where applicable) or a designated Grievance Officer / person able to answer Data Principals' questions and redress personal-data grievances expeditiously.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Privacy Policy & Grievance Officer Disclosure

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Privacy Policy or Grievance page specifies a designated Grievance Officer / DPO / official contact channel for data-protection queries.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Privacy Policy exists but provides no grievance contact or points only to a generic 'Contact Us' without redressal process.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No data grievance officer or privacy contact channel observed on a portal collecting citizen data.
benign_explanations: Full DPDP Act Sec 8(9)-(10) enforcement commences 13 May 2027; many government portals currently route data queries via WIM or Public Grievance Officer.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: DPDP Act 2023 Section 8(5)–(7); DPDP Rules 2025 Rules 6–7 & Second Schedule (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.title: Reasonable Security Safeguards, Retention Limits and Data Breach Intimation Controls
checkpoints.requirement_text: Backend data protection engineering, access controls, retention schedules, and breach-notification processes for citizen databases.
checkpoints.conformance_level: Statutory Privacy Mandate (IT Act / DPDP Act 2023)
checkpoints.citation: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 & DPDP Rules, 2025 · DPDP Act 2023 Section 8(5)–(7); DPDP Rules 2025 Rules 6–7 & Second Schedule (enforceable 13.05.2027)
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Backend database/security architecture — not observable via public web crawl.
checkpoints.caveats: Backend database security, retention deletion schedules, and incident-response workflows are strictly internal and cannot be audited from public HTML.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires internal security architecture, DPIA/audit, and data-retention governance review. Partial/stale: Not determinable from public web pages.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Data Fiduciaries (including State instrumentalities under Section 7(b) and Second Schedule of the DPDP Rules, 2025) must implement reasonable security safeguards (encryption, access controls, logging), enforce purpose-bound retention/erasure, and notify DPBI and affected Data Principals upon personal data breaches.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Security & Backend Data Governance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires internal security architecture, DPIA/audit, and data-retention governance review.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from public web pages.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: Internal technical safeguards are managed within NIC/MeitY/State cloud infrastructure.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: Policy on Open Standards for e-Governance (Nov 2010), Section 4 & Clauses 4.1.1–4.1.5
checkpoints.title: Open Web Markup Free of Deprecated/Proprietary Browser Plugins (Flash, Silverlight, ActiveX, Java Applets)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Public `.gov.in` web pages must rely on open web standards (HTML5/CSS/JS) and MUST NOT depend on obsolete/proprietary browser plugins such as Adobe Flash (`.swf`), Microsoft Silverlight, Java Applets (`<applet>`), or ActiveX controls (`clsid:` / `application/x-shockwave-flash`).
checkpoints.conformance_level: Mandatory GoI Open Standards / NDSAP Policy
checkpoints.citation: MeitY Policy on Open Standards for e-Governance · Policy on Open Standards for e-Governance (Nov 2010), Section 4 & Clauses 4.1.1–4.1.5
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Absence of `<applet>`, `<embed>`/`<object>` with `application/x-shockwave-flash`, `.swf`, `application/x-silverlight`, `application/x-java-applet`, or ActiveX `classid='clsid:...'` on sampled HTML.
checkpoints.caveats: Passive HTML tag/attribute inspection cleanly identifies legacy Flash/Silverlight/ActiveX/Applet embeds.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Zero deprecated proprietary browser plugins (Flash/SWF, Silverlight, Java Applet, ActiveX) observed on sampled HTML pages. Partial/stale: Legacy `<object>` Flash fallback exists inside HTML alongside modern HTML5 content.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Section 4 mandates adoption of Single and Royalty-Free Open Standards (Clauses 4.1.1–4.1.5: open specification, royalty-free patent claims, not-for-profit collaborative maintenance, technology-neutral implementation) to ensure long-term interoperability and avoid proprietary vendor lock-in.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Open Standards, Cross-Browser Compatibility & Technology Neutrality

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Zero deprecated proprietary browser plugins (Flash/SWF, Silverlight, Java Applet, ActiveX) observed on sampled HTML pages.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Legacy `<object>` Flash fallback exists inside HTML alongside modern HTML5 content.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Deprecated proprietary plugin embed (Flash `.swf`, Silverlight, Java Applet, or ActiveX `clsid:`) observed on landing page.
benign_explanations: Old unmaintained microsites or archival banners sometimes retain dormant `<embed>` tags.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: MeitY Open Standards Policy (2010) & GIGW Document Metadata / Open-Format Download Practice
checkpoints.title: Downloadable Document Links Declare File Format, Size and Language Metadata (Avoid Proprietary-Only Locks)
checkpoints.requirement_text: When a `.gov.in` page links to downloadable documents (`.pdf`, `.doc`, `.docx`, `.xls`, `.xlsx`, `.ods`, `.odt`, `.csv`, `.zip`), check whether link text/context discloses file type and file size (e.g., `(PDF, 420 KB)`), and note proprietary-only binary formats (`.doc`/`.xls`/`.rar`).
checkpoints.conformance_level: Mandatory GoI Open Standards / NDSAP Policy
checkpoints.citation: MeitY Policy on Open Standards for e-Governance · MeitY Open Standards Policy (2010) & GIGW Document Metadata / Open-Format Download Practice
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: For sampled document download `<a>` links, inspect anchor text / adjacent parent text for file-size unit (`KB`/`MB`) and format label (`PDF`/`CSV`/etc.), plus flag proprietary `.rar`/legacy `.doc`.
checkpoints.caveats: Applicable only when sampled pages contain downloadable document links; mark not_applicable when page has zero document downloads.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Document download links disclose file format and size metadata (e.g., 'PDF, 350 KB') and use open/accessible formats. Partial/stale: Some downloads list format/size metadata while others provide bare untitled links or legacy `.doc`/`.rar` files.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Publicly downloadable documents should adhere to open, accessible formats (HTML, accessible PDF, ODF/CSV) rather than proprietary-only archives without open alternatives, and download links should indicate file format, size, and language to aid bandwidth-constrained and assistive-tech users.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW 3.0 Quality & Accessibility — File Type, Size & Language on Download Links

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Document download links disclose file format and size metadata (e.g., 'PDF, 350 KB') and use open/accessible formats.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Some downloads list format/size metadata while others provide bare untitled links or legacy `.doc`/`.rar` files.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Document download links present on sampled pages without file-size or format metadata.
benign_explanations: CMS download tables sometimes display file size in an adjacent table column rather than inside the `<a>` tag itself.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: NDSAP 2012 (Gazette of India, 17.03.2012) — Machine-Readable Open Government Data & data.gov.in
checkpoints.title: Machine-Readable Open Data Availability (CSV/JSON/XML/ODS) or Official Open Data (data.gov.in) Link
checkpoints.requirement_text: Observe whether data-publishing `.gov.in` portals expose machine-readable open formats (`.csv`, `.json`, `.xml`, `.ods`) or link to the national Open Government Data portal (`data.gov.in`) / Open APIs (`apisetu.gov.in`).
checkpoints.conformance_level: Mandatory GoI Open Standards / NDSAP Policy
checkpoints.citation: National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy · NDSAP 2012 (Gazette of India, 17.03.2012) — Machine-Readable Open Government Data & data.gov.in
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Outbound link to `data.gov.in` / `apisetu.gov.in` OR Open Data / Datasets section OR direct `.csv`/`.json`/`.xml`/`.ods` public data links.
checkpoints.caveats: Applies meaningfully to ministries, statistical/scheme agencies, and data-holding public bodies; informational microsites without statistical datasets may legitimately have no open data exports.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Portal links to `data.gov.in` / Open Data section or publishes downloadable machine-readable open datasets (CSV/JSON/XML/ODS). Partial/stale: Publishes statistical tables exclusively as locked/scanned PDFs without CSV/Excel/ODS machine-readable downloads.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: NDSAP-2012 facilitates proactive access to Government of India-owned shareable non-sensitive data generated using public funds in both human-readable and machine-readable open formats (CSV, XML, JSON, ODS) through an all-India network including the Open Government Data Platform (data.gov.in).
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: GIGW Open Data & NDSAP Interoperability

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Portal links to `data.gov.in` / Open Data section or publishes downloadable machine-readable open datasets (CSV/JSON/XML/ODS).
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Publishes statistical tables exclusively as locked/scanned PDFs without CSV/Excel/ODS machine-readable downloads.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: No `data.gov.in` link, Open Data section, or machine-readable dataset link observed on sampled pages.
benign_explanations: Ministry/department may publish its NDSAP datasets directly on `data.gov.in` without placing a backlink on every subdomain.
Small administrative offices may hold no shareable statistical datasets.

checkpoints.section_name: MeitY, CERT-In/STQC, IT Act/DPDP & Open Standards
checkpoints.serial_no: NDSAP 2012 — Chief Data Officer (CDO), Negative/Positive List Classification & Periodic Dataset Releases
checkpoints.title: Institutional NDSAP Data Governance (Chief Data Officer, Data Classification & data.gov.in Publishing)
checkpoints.requirement_text: Internal institutional governance for classifying shareable vs restricted data, maintaining metadata standards, and assigning a Chief Data Officer.
checkpoints.conformance_level: Mandatory GoI Open Standards / NDSAP Policy
checkpoints.citation: National Data Sharing and Accessibility Policy · NDSAP 2012 — Chief Data Officer (CDO), Negative/Positive List Classification & Periodic Dataset Releases
checkpoints.public_disclosure_indicator: Internal governance process; CDO directory is maintained on data.gov.in.
checkpoints.caveats: Internal ministerial data classification and CDO roster management are administered via DST/NIC (`data.gov.in`) and cannot be audited solely from department homepages.
checkpoints.agent_inspection_guidance: Requires verifying CDO designation and departmental dataset cataloguing on data.gov.in / DST records. Partial/stale: Not determinable from department landing page HTML.
checkpoints.statutory_text_excerpt: Under NDSAP 2012 Implementation Guidelines, each Ministry/Department designates a Chief Data Officer (CDO) / Data Controller to classify datasets into open/registered/restricted (negative) lists, maintain standardised metadata, and periodically upload open datasets to data.gov.in.
checkpoints.gigw_cross_reference: N/A — Institutional NDSAP Data Governance

agent_inspection_rubric.observed_criteria: Requires verifying CDO designation and departmental dataset cataloguing on data.gov.in / DST records.
agent_inspection_rubric.partial_or_stale_criteria: Not determinable from department landing page HTML.
agent_inspection_rubric.not_observed_criteria: Classify as internal_governance.
benign_explanations: CDO rosters are published centrally on data.gov.in rather than every department website.
